gaps.title: No country selector; flat 10-15 digit rule; identity is the last 10 digits of whatever was typed
gaps.scenario: A participant in Singapore (8-digit numbers), UAE/Saudi/Israel (9-digit), or anywhere outside India types their national number. z.js:89 has one mobile box with an Indian placeholder and no country control; phone-runtime.ts:293 sends only the raw string; worker.ts:1489 rejects anything under 10 digits ('Enter a valid mobile number.'). The guide then tells them to 'type the 10-digit number' and 'add the country code only if outside India' (guide.js:86-87). Even when accepted, identity = last 10 digits (worker.ts:1493, people.ts:48), so a UAE employee who types the normal local form 050 123 4567 (last10 0501234567) does NOT match a list entry uploaded as +971 50 123 4567 (last10 1501234567); the same happens for France (06...), Australia (04...), Saudi (05...). In a list game they land in the waiting room; in an open game they get a ticket under a number the organizer cannot match. Different countries can also share the same last 10 digits and be treated as one person.
gaps.recommendation: Add a Country <select> (full ISO list with dial code, default India) in front of every mobile box on z.html (ship a small data table: ISO, dial code, min/max national digits, trunk-prefix rule; common.js TB.COUNTRIES has only 31 countries and no lengths, and is not loaded by z.html). Take the national number, strip +CC/00CC/trunk 0 for that country, show 'India: 10 digits' and a live counter, send {country, phone}. Server: normalise to E.164 and key identity on the full E.164 (keep a dual lookup against the legacy last-10 hash so existing lists still match; apply the same normaliser in cleanPhone/list upload and in the check-in/winner-confirm mobile edits). Rewrite the guide.js mobile entries (86-87, 182) without '10-digit' and 'outside India'.

gaps.title: No mandatory/optional markers on any field
gaps.scenario: The owner wants a small red asterisk plus the word 'mandatory' on compulsory fields and '(optional)' on optional ones. joinWho/joinView (z.js:87-110) render plain labels; the inputs have no required/aria-required/data-need; z.css has no marker style. A participant cannot tell that the ID box in 'both + employees only' is compulsory, that 'Your employee ID (employees only)' can be left empty, or that the name box does not need to be filled.
gaps.recommendation: Add helpers req(label)/opt(label) producing '*mandatory' (red, AA contrast, small font) and '(optional)', apply per the target table, add required/aria-required on mandatory inputs and data-need so guide.js hintDisabled (guide.js:431-444) names the missing fields, and mark the two consent boxes mandatory too. Add DOM tests per verify/employeesOnly combination asserting the marker text.

gaps.title: ID-only mode cannot take the mobile number as an optional field
gaps.scenario: Verify = employee ID only. With employees-only on, the form shows only the ID box and the mobile cannot be given at all (z.js:91); with it off, the mobile box is an alternative for non-employees ('No employee ID? Type your mobile number instead'), not an optional extra. The owner wants the mobile shown as '(optional)' beside a mandatory ID. Even if the box were added, the server drops it: listed-by-ID people carry no phone (people.ts:290-295), 'either' ignores a typed phone once the ID matches (worker.ts:1579), and id mode uses the phone as the identity (see next gap). The check-in screen then forces an ID-only participant to tick 'This mobile number is correct' for an empty box (z.js:726-727, checkin.ts:88).
gaps.recommendation: In id mode always show Employee ID (mandatory) and Mobile (optional, with country). Server: resolve identity by ID first (as 'either' does at worker.ts:1575-1580) and, when a phone is typed, store it in the sealed pii.phone for prize hand-over without using it as the identity. In checkin hide the mobile row (or show 'No mobile number given') when pii.phone is empty and relax confirmMobile accordingly.

gaps.title: id mode: a listed employee who fills BOTH the ID and the mobile box is sent to the waiting room
gaps.scenario: Audience 6 (anyone, employees confirm with ID) or any id-mode game that is not employees-only shows both boxes. People listed by ID are stored with identity empHashOf(ID) (people.ts:290-295). If the employee types ID and mobile, idOnly is false (worker.ts:1581), ph becomes the PHONE hash (1583), personByPhone finds nothing (1611), the id-mode branch marks idMiss (1615) and wait() runs (1665): the employee sees 'Please wait a moment ... This engagement is by invitation', is counted against the 30-per-10-minutes ID-miss limit, and the organizer must admit a person who was already on the list. After admission a second person row keyed by phone is created and the listed row stays 'Invited'. No test sends ID and phone together to an id-mode game.
gaps.recommendation: For id mode (and the form's mixed audiences) look the ID up first, exactly like the 'either' branch, and treat a typed phone as an attribute not an identity. Add edge tests: id mode with ID only, phone only, both, wrong ID + right phone; and a DOM test that fills #emp and #ph together.

gaps.title: Name is always asked, never marked, and the list name is never used visibly
gaps.scenario: Requirement: ask the name unless the organizer/host already supplied it for that ID, then use it as is. Today the Name box is shown in every non-personal case (z.js:110) with no marker and no hint; the server keeps the list name and ignores the typed one when the list has a name (worker.ts:1663), and never requires a name at all (cleanName may return empty). The page cannot show the list name after the ID is typed (no lookup endpoint) and gives no 'we already have your name' confirmation; the stored name is first visible only in the optional check-in step (checkin.ts:82). Result: people type a name that is thrown away, or leave it empty and the organizer sees a blank row.
gaps.recommendation: Decide the rule with the owner and implement both halves: (1) server returns code 'need-name' (400) only when the matched list row has no name and none was typed (the page then reveals a mandatory Name box), or a rate-limited, consent-gated lookup returns a masked/first name for the typed ID so the page can show 'Welcome, Asha' and hide the box (weigh the enumeration risk noted at worker.ts:1624); (2) show a mandatory/optional marker on the Name box and echo the stored name after joining. Keep personal links greeting by first name (the OG page already does, people.ts:639).

gaps.title: UNCONFIRMED: guide.js likely rewrites the waiting-room card into an error panel

Your request is with the organizer...'. guide.js MSGSEL includes [role=status] (376); upgrade() (387-399) matches the fragment 'This engagement is by invitation' (guide.js:95, kind blocked), replaces the card in place with the red .ctg-inline panel titled 'This game is by invitation' and the steps 'Please ask the Organizer ... to add your mobile number. All join/waiting tests omit guide.js, so nothing would catch this. Not executed; derived by reading.
gaps.recommendation: Open /z in a real browser with a list-only game and a number not on the list to confirm. Fix: exempt the waiting/declined/lapsed/removed/gone cards (e.g. data-ctg-skip checked in okToUpgrade/leafMessage) or drop role=status on them, and give 'This game is by invitation' a player-specific text in PLAYER_TEXT. Add a test that loads guide.js and asserts the waiting card still reads 'Please wait a moment' with the Type-it-again button.

gaps.title: No 'nothing required' option: mobile is mandatory even in an 'anyone can join' game
gaps.scenario: The owner lists 'none of the above / anyone can join' and 'join without any validation'. VERIFY_MODES has no 'none' (config.ts:130); an anyone-game with verify mobile still returns 'Enter a valid mobile number.' for a blank box (worker.ts:1584). Any 10-15 digit string is accepted, so the 'validation' is cosmetic, yet a real number is collected from people who may not want to give one.
gaps.recommendation: Owner decision. If a no-contact mode is wanted: add verify 'none' (name only, identity = device + ticket), a K4 wording variant without mobile, prize hand-over by name/ticket number, and hide the mobile box on the page. If not, say plainly on the page why the number is needed and keep it as the one mandatory field with the marker.

gaps.title: Page does not use whoCanJoin; invited-by banner contradicts the waiting-room reality
gaps.scenario: info already returns whoCanJoin (worker.ts:1784) but noteInfo ignores it (z.js:41-49), so a list game and an open game show the identical form. For ANY from= link (organizer, Host, Co-host or guest) the page says 'You were invited by a colleague or family member. Join with your own mobile number to get your own ticket.' In list games (audiences 2 and 4, where guest invites exist) a non-listed invitee always waits for approval (worker.ts:1665), so the promise is false; in ID modes it names the wrong field; for Organizer/Host/Co-host links it names the wrong inviter.
gaps.recommendation: Read whoCanJoin (and the from= kind via the same code ranges as people.ts:27-29, 84-92) and show one accurate line: open game 'Type your details to get your ticket'; list game 'This game is for invited people. If you are on the list you get your ticket straight away, otherwise your request goes to <organizer / the person who invited you>'. Mode-aware wording (ID vs mobile).

gaps.title: Copy is hard-wired to 'mobile number' in ID modes and consent does not mention the employee ID
gaps.scenario: Step chip 2 says 'Type your number' in every mode (z.js:105); the footer says 'We use your number for your ticket...' For privacy-minimal ID-only games the footer and K4-A describe data that was not collected and omit data that was.
gaps.recommendation: Build the step chip, footer and needPhone texts from the mode (ID / mobile / both). Add a K4 wording variant (or generic 'my details') that names the employee ID, bump TERMS_VERSION in both consent.js:6 and apps/edge/src/brand.ts:6 together, and keep consent-text.json in step.

gaps.title: needPhone state loops for an ID-only person
gaps.scenario: A personal link already used on another phone puts the page in needPhone. In ID games the form leads with the employee ID, and bindJoin accepts an ID alone (J.emp non-empty, line 835), but the token is still sent and the server resolves the identity from the token's person (ph = tok.ph, worker.ts:1583), so it answers link-used (423) again. The banner and the blank-input message only talk about a mobile number.
gaps.recommendation: In needPhone, if an ID is typed, drop the token from the request (or let the server resolve by ID) and word the banner and messages for the mode; otherwise hide the ID box in that state.

gaps.title: Typo in an ID or number is treated as an invitation request with misleading text; shared-office limit
gaps.scenario: An employee who mistypes their own ID or number is told 'This engagement is by invitation' and 'Your request is with the organizer' (worker.ts:1660), even in a game that is open to anyone; the organizer's waiting list fills with typo requests. The ID-miss limit of 30 per 10 minutes is per network address per game (1616-1621): hundreds of staff behind one office NAT can lock each other out with 'Too many tries with an employee ID that is not on the list.'
gaps.recommendation: Before sending to the waiting room, show a confirmation ('We will ask the organizer to admit EMP-1042. Is that right?') or echo the entered value back; reword the message for typos in anyone-games; raise or key the ID-miss limit per game rather than per address, or per (address, ID) pair.

gaps.title: Indian-number rule exists for lists but not at join
gaps.scenario: List upload requires a 10-digit Indian mobile to start with 6-9 (people.ts:71) and rejects letters (people.ts:64), but join accepts any 10-15 digits and ignores letters. '5123456789' or 'abc9876543210x' produce a ticket in an open game and a waiting request in a list game, with no warning.
gaps.recommendation: Use the same per-country normaliser/validator for join and upload once the country selector exists; reject letters and impossible leading digits with a country-specific message.

gaps.title: No client-side validation; errors arrive only as a banner after a server round trip
gaps.scenario: A blank or short mobile, a blank ID or an ID with bad characters is only reported after the request; the field is not marked invalid (no aria-invalid / aria-describedby), the banner is placed under the name box, and focus moves only because guide.js outlines the box. Screen-reader and slow-network users get a late, detached message.
gaps.recommendation: Validate length, characters and mandatory state on input/blur, show the message directly under the field, set aria-invalid and aria-describedby, and keep the server messages as the fallback.

gaps.title: Check-in screen: ID-only participants must confirm a blank mobile; mobile edit accepts Indian numbers only
gaps.scenario: The check-in form always shows 'Your mobile number' plus a mandatory tick 'This mobile number is correct' (z.js:726-727; checkin.ts:88 requires confirmMobile) even when no mobile exists. If the participant edits it, the server accepts only ^[6-9]\d{9}$ after stripping 91/0 (checkin.ts:103-104) and answers 'The mobile number needs 10 digits', so a participant abroad cannot correct a non-Indian number; the guide repeats '10 digits' (guide.js:47).
gaps.recommendation: Reuse the new country-aware normaliser in check-in (and in the winner confirm card, z.js:317), hide or relabel the mobile row when none is held, and drop the tick requirement for an empty mobile.

gaps.title: Typed values and ticks are lost on reload or app switch; redraw guard checks only one box
gaps.scenario: J.phone/J.emp/J.name and the K4 ticks live only in memory (z.js:84); a participant who switches to WhatsApp to copy an ID and comes back after the tab was reclaimed starts again. paint() skips a redraw only if the first of #ph/#nm/#emp that exists is focused (776); in employees-only ID mode that is #nm, so a redraw while typing in #emp would wipe it (latent: redraws on the join screen are rare).
gaps.recommendation: Persist the typed ID/phone/name (not the ticks) in sessionStorage for the join screen, and make the focus guard test any focused input inside the form.

gaps.title: Game name, organizer and start time are not shown on the join form
gaps.scenario: The page shows only the brand strip and 'Join the engagement'. info.name is returned but unused, and the installed app reopens the last game kept on the phone (z.js:9), so a person can join an old or wrong game without noticing; a personal-link holder is not greeted although the share preview is.
gaps.recommendation: Show the game name (and start time in the phone's zone) in the join card header and greet personal-link holders by first name if the server can return it safely.

gaps.title: Rate limits per network address hit offices and look like a server fault
gaps.scenario: JOIN_PER_IP_MINUTE is 200 and JOIN_PER_IP_DAY 1500 (388-396). A 1,000-person all-hands behind one company NAT, all joining in the 2-minute set-up window, exceeds 200 per minute; the extra people get 'It is busy right now. Please try again in a few minutes.' The guide classes it as 'Something did not work on our side' with a WhatsApp button and no Try again button on this page (guide.js:206; z.js:855 sets the retry hook only on the boot screen).
gaps.recommendation: Raise or make the per-minute limit game-aware (or count only after a game-size multiple), give 429 busy its own 'wait' guide with a working Try again, and keep the Retry-after hint on the form.

gaps.title: Waiting-room polling has no jitter or back-off
gaps.scenario: Every waiting phone polls /me?wid every 5 seconds from the moment of joining (setInterval 5000, no jitter, no slow-down); a list game with hundreds of waiting people produces a synchronous burst of tens of requests per second on the free-plan Worker/D1.
gaps.recommendation: Add per-phone jitter, back off to 15-30 s after the first minute, and prefer the existing public-file pattern (a published admit list or SSE) for large waiting rooms.

gaps.title: Guide copy and a few labels are wrong or imprecise for ID and global use
gaps.scenario: The ID guide says 'Letters and numbers only' though dots, dashes, underscores and slashes are allowed (people.ts:51) and, for 'both + employees only', suggests typing a mobile number instead of the ID. 'Your name (shown only to the organizer)' (z.js:110) is also visible to Hosts in their people list. 'Players are 18 or older.' (z.js:114) repeats consent box B.
gaps.recommendation: Tighten the catalog entries per mode, reword the name label ('visible to your organizer and hosts only'), and drop the duplicate 18+ line.

gaps.title: Accessibility details on the join form
gaps.scenario:
The whole #app is aria-live=polite (z.html:7), so each innerHTML redraw is announced; hints are plain

not tied to inputs; the only format hint for the phone is an Indian placeholder; the ID box has no format example; errors are not linked to fields.
gaps.recommendation: Link hints and errors with aria-describedby, give the ID box an example placeholder from the organizer's list format if available, and avoid re-announcing the whole form (limit aria-live to the error banner).

gaps.title: Shared phone: one ticket per device blocks a second family member
gaps.scenario: Two people sharing one phone (or one browser profile) cannot both join: the second gets 409 'This phone already holds a ticket in this engagement. One phone, one ticket...'. iOS home-screen apps and private windows have separate storage from the browser, so a returning player may be told their ticket is 'in a different browser or app' (423).
gaps.recommendation: Product decision: keep the rule but state it on the join form (one line) and in the invitation texts; for lost-storage cases offer the organizer 'move ticket' hint earlier or a re-bind code.

gaps.title: No DOM test covers the employee-ID boxes or the guide on the join screens
gaps.scenario: The join page tests load only audio.js, zgame.js and z.js (consent.js is added by the harness, guide.js is not) and only drive #ph/#nm. Nothing types into #emp, nothing combines #emp and #ph, nothing asserts markers, and nothing checks what the guide does to the waiting card, so the two defects above (id-mode both typed; guide rewrite) pass unnoticed.
gaps.recommendation: Add a join-matrix DOM suite: every verify x employeesOnly x (anyone/list) x (personal/common/guest link) combination, with guide.js loaded, asserting visible fields, labels, markers, each wrong-input message, the waiting/declined/lapsed screens and that the page stays on 'Please wait a moment'.

analyses.findings:
SCOPE AND METHOD
Read in full: apps/edge/src/worker.ts (join route 1558-1680 plus digitsOf/phoneHash 1489-1494, joinOverLimit 388-396, unbind 1745-1755, person/forget 1723-1744, mark 1891-1903, roster/reuse 1958-1997, settings 1998-2038, create 1388-1406, info 1783, summary 1825, pub() 104), apps/edge/src/people.ts (all), apps/edge/src/checkin.ts, apps/edge/src/consent.ts, apps/edge/src/pii.ts, packages/beacon/src/config.ts, apps/edge/test/verify.test.ts, and, only to learn what the page sends, apps/web/public/z.js (join form 87-112, handler 824-842, api wrapper 51-61), packages/beacon/src/phone-runtime.ts join() (291), apps/web/public/zc.js organizer help text. Working tree is 1.2.0 (uncommitted: local.ts latency knob and a 2-line z.js change; neither touches join logic). No code was run.

A. WHAT THE PAGE SENDS (so the server rows below are reachable)
POST /api/z/{id}/join body = { phone (always sent, may be ""), name, empId (only if non-empty), device (random 32 hex kept in localStorage ctz:device), from+cat (common/guest link), token (personal link, added by the api wrapper), consent {v, boxes:[A,B]} (K4) }. There is NO country field and NO other field. GET /info returns verify ("number" when default, else id/either/both - the page maps "number" to "mobile"), employeesOnly, whoCanJoin. Nothing in info says which field is mandatory or optional, and nothing says whether a name is already on file.

B. EXACT ORDER OF THE JOIN DECISION (worker.ts)
0 game state: unknown id 404 "No such engagement."; did-not-start 403 code did-not-start; cancelled 403 code cancelled; draft 403 "This engagement is not open yet." (no code). Unpaid-and-late (locked) does NOT block joining (only mails the organizer). There is no "game ended" check anywhere in join.
1 token (if sent): person looked up by hash; unknown / malformed / removed -> 404 code link-gone "This link is not valid any more. Please ask the person who invited you to send it again."
2 phone (if non-blank): digitsOf = strip every non-digit, accept only 10..15 digits, else 400 "Enter a valid mobile number." (no code, no reason). Hash = sha(salt|last 10 digits).
3 empId: normEmp = drop spaces, UPPER, must match ^[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9._-/]{0,29}$ else 400 code bad-id "An employee ID has letters and numbers only." (message does not mention the 30-character limit or that . _ - / are allowed).
4 employees-only checks (skipped when a token is present): mode id or both and no ID -> 400 need-id ("Enter your employee ID." for id; "Enter your employee ID and your mobile number." for both). Mode either and neither given -> 400 need-id "Enter your mobile number or your employee ID."
5 mode either + ID typed + no token: ID looked up first (person keyed by ID hash, or the idx/ alias to a phone-keyed person). Hit = the person is adopted as if they had used their personal link and the typed phone is DISCARDED.
6 identity: idOnly = (mode id or either) AND ID typed AND phone NOT typed AND no token -> identity = hash of the ID. Otherwise identity = hash of the typed phone, else the token's person. No identity -> 400 (no code) with a mode text: id "Enter your employee ID, or your mobile number if you have no employee ID."; either "Enter your mobile number or your employee ID."; mobile AND both "Enter a valid mobile number."
7 returning participant (participant row with this identity): removed seat -> 403 code removed "You were removed from this game by the organizer."; K4 never ticked -> 400 consent-required; seat bound to another device -> 423 (code link-used + needPhone:true if a token and no typed phone, else code other-phone); seat with no device (organizer unbound / list seat) and this device already holds another seat -> 409 device-used; otherwise the first device keeps the seat (binds dev, may fill an empty name), 200 { pid, again:true, jr, ... }.
8 new person: person = personByPhone(identity). Mode id/either, ID typed, no token: not on a list -> idMiss. Mode both, ID typed: phone not listed, or listed with a DIFFERENT ID -> idMiss (a list entry with no ID accepts any typed ID, and the typed ID is not stored). idMiss counts one try against 30 per network per game per 10-minute bucket; the 31st -> 429 code too-many-tries "Too many tries with an employee ID that is not on the list. Please ask your organizer for help." (the counter moves BEFORE the consent and removed checks, and also on every retry or reload of the same wrong ID). Mode both, phone listed with an ID, no ID typed: remembered as needIdAfterConsent.
9 listed person with status removed -> 403 removed. K4 missing and not ticked before -> 400 consent-required "Please tick the box to continue." Then needIdAfterConsent -> 400 need-id "Enter your employee ID."
10 no device id -> 400 "Please refresh this page and try again." (no code). Device already holds a seat -> 409 device-used "This phone already holds a ticket ... One phone, one ticket." Participants >= cap -> 409 "This engagement is full." (no code; counts participants only).
11 owner of the link (only matters when the person is on no list): personal-link-with-other-number -> the link owner's chain; from=org -> organizer; from=host/cohost -> that key's list if the key is live, else organizer; from=guest -> that guest only if guest invitations are on and that guest was not themselves invited by a guest; no/invalid from -> organizer.
12 not on a list: whoCanJoin=list (or employees-only, which forces list) OR idMiss -> waiting room (see C). Else if the owner has a limit (Co-host default 100 per game, guest 1-10 per person) and that list is full -> waiting room flagged overlimit (409 code invite-full "This invitation has already been used by N people..."). Else direct join under the owner.
13 per-network new-seat limits (200/minute, 1,500/day, same counter for waiting): over -> 429 code busy "It is busy right now. Please try again in a few minutes."; daily write budget -> 503 busy.
14 addSeat (one batch): seat + participant + person row, guards for cap, owner limit and device; a lost race maps to device-used, invite-full waiting, or "full".

C. WAITING ROOM (addWaiting people.ts 604-614; decideWaiting 507-531; decideAll 534-572; me?wid 585-592)
Answer to the asker: HTTP 403 code waiting { waiting:true, wid, with } "This engagement is by invitation. Your request is with {the organizer | the host name | the co-host name | the person who invited you}. You can come in as soon as they say yes." (the wording says "by invitation" even when the game is open to anyone and the cause is an unlisted employee ID). Same identity asking again returns the SAME row: declined -> 403 code declined (permanent for that number/ID); waiting/admitted -> the waiting answer again. Max 500 waiting rows per game (429 code waiting-full). Stored: one waiting row (identity hash, sealed {phone,name,empId}, via, inviter, chain, overlimit) + one K4 consent row; no seat, no participant. Admit: creates a person row (status invited, approved_by) only when none exists, or revives a removed one; an EXISTING non-removed person row is left alone and the waiting row is just marked admitted. The page then polls me?wid every 5 s and re-sends the join with the same typed values.

D. WHAT EACH CONFIGURATION MAKES MANDATORY ON THE SERVER (name is NEVER required in any path)
mode mobile (default), any who-can-join: mobile required (valid 10-15 digits). ID ignored, but still format-checked.
mode id, employees-only: ID required (need-id). Mobile: the page offers no field; the server would accept it but it changes identity (gap 2).
mode id, not employees-only: ID or mobile required (either one). Both typed -> mobile wins (gap 2).
mode either: ID or mobile required (either; need-id code only when employees-only). Both typed -> ID wins if the ID is on a list, else mobile.
mode both, employees-only: mobile AND ID required.
mode both, not employees-only: mobile required; ID required ONLY if the listed record for that mobile holds an ID (asked after consent); an unlisted outsider may leave it empty; an ID typed by an unlisted person sends them to the waiting room.
Employees-only also forces closed=1 (list only) and switches guest invitations off. Turning employees-only off later leaves closed=1 unless whoCanJoin is also sent.

E. DECISION TABLE (condensed; the full row set is in the data field). L = listed, U = not listed, status/code/message as sent.
MOBILE MODE: nothing -> 400 "Enter a valid mobile number." | bad number -> same text, no reason | L -> 200, seat+participant (list name used as is; typed name stored only if list name empty), person->joined, K4 | U + anyone -> 200 direct, person row under link owner, phone stored AS TYPED (no country code), typed name | U + list/employees-only -> 403 waiting | removed -> 403 removed.
ID MODE: nothing -> 400 need-id (employees-only) or text without code (open) | ID only, L by ID -> 200 (identity = ID, phone kept if the list had one, mobile optional works) | ID only, U -> 403 waiting in EVERY who-can-join setting | ID + mobile, L by ID -> 403 waiting (gap 2) | mobile only, L by phone -> 200 | mobile only, L by ID -> not recognised: stranger seat (anyone) or waiting (list) | mobile only, U -> 200 (anyone) / waiting (list).
EITHER MODE: ID only, L -> 200 same ticket as via mobile | ID only, U -> waiting | mobile only L -> 200; U -> 200 or waiting | ID + mobile: ID listed -> that person (typed mobile thrown away); ID unlisted but mobile listed -> that person (typed ID ignored); both unlisted -> waiting even in an open game.
BOTH MODE: mobile only L-with-ID -> 400 need-id (after consent) | mobile only L-without-ID or U(anyone) -> 200 | mobile + right ID -> 200 | mobile listed with ID X, typed ID Y -> waiting; organizer Admit does nothing useful (endless re-wait, gap 3) | mobile unlisted + ID -> waiting | ID only -> 400 "Enter a valid mobile number." (does not mention the ID or that both are needed).
LINKS: personal link alone -> 200 for any mode, skips every ID/mobile rule (strong proof), binds the first device; other device -> 423 link-used needPhone; link + a different typed number -> that stranger is queued/admitted under the link owner; removed or unknown token -> 404 link-gone. Common link (from=): affects only unlisted people (owner and limit). Guest link when guest invitations are off, when the inviter was guest-invited, or a revoked Host/Co-host key -> silently lands under the organizer.
RETURNING / SECOND PHONE / RELOAD: same identity + same device -> 200 again:true (no consent needed if ever ticked). Same identity, other browser/profile/phone, or site data cleared -> 423 other-phone "A ticket plays on one device only ... ask your organizer to move your ticket to this phone." Organizer paths: People list "send link again" (works for every listed person, ID-keyed too) or the console "Change of phone" box, which takes a MOBILE number only (unbind: phone or seat number). Reload on the play screen sends no join (pid kept on the phone); reload on the waiting screen is restored from the phone and resumes polling; reload on the join form loses the K4 ticks (page) but the server remembers consent.

F. WHAT IS STORED
Listed join: seat(ph hash, dev hash, jr, inv, src), participant(phone_hash, sealed {p,n,e}), person status joined, K4 row. Direct join adds a person row too (inviter = link owner) with the same sealed blob. Waiting: waiting row + K4 (subject = pidOf(identity)). Counters in kv: jbm/jlim per network hash (every new seat or waiting request) and idmiss per network hash per 10 minutes. Names/numbers/IDs only inside AES-GCM blobs; identity hashes use PHONE_SALT; pid is derived from the identity hash. The phone inside the blob is: list entry = cleanPhone digits WITH country code (91...); direct joiner = digits exactly as typed (10 digits, or 12 if they typed +91); ID-only = "". Employee ID stored only when the mode is not mobile and the person is ID-keyed or a direct joiner with an ID (in mode both the typed ID of a listed person is NOT stored).

G. PHONE / COUNTRY HANDLING TODAY (three different rule sets)
List entry (people.ts cleanPhone 62-77): letters/symbols rejected; +cc or 00cc accepted at 8-15 digits for any non-91 country; 10 digits must start 6-9 (India-only message otherwise); +91 needs exactly 10 more digits; 11-15 digit numbers without + accepted as international. Digits always carry the country code.
Join (worker.ts digitsOf 1489): any text, non-digits silently dropped, 10-15 digits, no prefix rule, no country. Roster/unbind/person/forget/mark use the same function.
Check-in edit (checkin.ts 103-104): after stripping a leading 91 or 0, must be ^[6-9]\d{9}$ - India only.
Matching key = last 10 digits only. That is consistent for India and for countries whose national number has 10+ digits, but for 8-9 digit national numbers (e.g. UAE, Spain, France, Singapore, Hong Kong, Netherlands, Australia, Israel) a listed +971501234567 hashes as 1501234567, so the person typing 0501234567 or 501234567 never matches, and anything under 10 digits is refused outright.

H. THINGS THAT WORK AS INTENDED
Server enforces K4 before keeping anything; K4 for waiting people is recorded; listed name wins over a typed one; personal link needs no typing; one device per ticket; removed people cannot come back; ID guessing is throttled; both-mode ID is asked only after consent so the consent box cannot be used to probe the list; ID alias in either mode keeps ID and phone as one ticket; export/resend keep the ID.

gaps.title: No country choice: join accepts only 10-15 digits, hashes last 10, stores digits as typed
gaps.scenario: A participant in Singapore (8-digit numbers), UAE/Spain/France/Netherlands/Australia (9 digits) types their normal national number: join answers 400 'Enter a valid mobile number.' with no reason and no hint to add a country code. If the organizer listed them as +971 50 123 4567 (hash of last 10 = 1501234567), typing 050 123 4567 or 0501234567 never matches the list, so they land in the waiting room or as a stranger. The page cannot send a country because the join body has no country field.
gaps.recommendation: Add a country/dial-code field (default IN) to the join body and to the people/roster/unbind/person/forget/mark/check-in routes. Server: one shared normaliser (extend cleanPhone) with a small per-country table {dial code, min and max national digits, India lead digit 6-9}; compose E.164 digits = dial code + national number (drop one leading trunk 0); validate the national length for that country; also accept a pasted +cc number by longest-prefix. Keep hashing the LAST 10 digits of the E.164 digits so hashes of already-listed numbers stay identical (list side already yields cc-bearing digits). Store the E.164 digits. Return specific reasons (too short for X, too long, India numbers start 6-9). Reject below 7-8 total digits. Join, roster and list must all call the same function so they cannot drift.

gaps.title: Typing the optional mobile number next to the employee ID throws a listed employee into the waiting room
gaps.scenario: Mode 'Employee ID' (page non-employees-only shows both an ID box and a mobile box; organizer help says 'A mobile number is optional'). Asha is listed by ID E101. She types E101 and her mobile. idOnly is false because a phone was typed, so identity becomes the PHONE hash; ID-keyed list entries are keyed by the ID hash, so personByPhone finds nothing, idMiss is set, she gets 403 'by invitation ... your request is with the organizer', and one of the 30 IP tries is burned (an office behind one network is locked out after 30 such people with 'Too many tries ...'). verify.test.ts only ever joins ID mode with phone undefined, so this is untested. The new page (mobile shown as optional next to the ID) would make this the common path.
gaps.recommendation: In modes id and either, if an ID is typed the identity must be the ID hash whatever else is typed; the typed mobile is only a contact number (validate with the shared normaliser, store in the sealed blob, never used for the lookup). Fall back to a phone-keyed match only when no ID is typed (or when the ID is unlisted AND the phone is a phone-keyed listed person). Add tests: id mode + ID + mobile, listed by ID, with and without phone on the list; either mode ID + mobile; both orders.

gaps.title: Organizer 'Admit' cannot rescue a mode-both person whose ID differs from the list: endless re-wait
gaps.scenario: Mode 'mobile and employee ID'. Ravi's mobile is listed with ID E102; he mistypes E120. Join: phone listed, ID differs -> idMiss -> waiting row keyed by his phone. Organizer presses Admit: decideWaiting finds an existing non-removed person row for that phone, so it only marks the waiting row admitted (no change to the person or its ID). The page sees state admitted, re-sends the join with E120, idMiss fires again, addWaiting returns the existing (admitted) row, and the server answers 403 waiting again. The page loops every 5 s, each loop spends write budget and an idmiss try, until 'Too many tries' appears after about 2.5 minutes. The organizer believes they approved him.
gaps.recommendation: Make approval authoritative: when a waiting row is admitted, remember it (approved_by/approved_ms on the person row is already available) and have join skip the ID check for a person whose waiting row is admitted (or overwrite the stored ID with the approved one). wait() must never answer 'waiting' for a row whose status is admitted. Also stop the page loop on a repeated waiting answer after admission and show a clear 'ask your organizer' text.

gaps.title: Unlisted employee IDs always wait, even when the game is open to anyone; console promises no approvals; message says 'by invitation'
gaps.scenario: Organizer chooses 'Anyone with the link, my employees confirm with their employee ID' (or any open game with ID/either/both). zc.js 798 tells them 'You do not need to approve anyone.' An employee whose ID is missing from the uploaded list, or who mistypes one character, gets 403 'This engagement is by invitation. Your request is with the organizer' and waits for a person who is not watching. The requirement that the page capture 'the minimum necessary' for 'ID only, anyone can join' has no server path that simply records the ID. Each distinct mistyped ID is a separate waiting row (verify.test.ts confirms 30 rows from 30 wrong IDs), 'Approve all' later admits those ghost IDs as invited persons, and 500 waiting rows (WAITING_MAX) block everyone else with 'Many people are waiting'.
gaps.recommendation: Make the unknown-ID behaviour an explicit setting (suggest default: in an open game an unknown ID is admitted and its ID recorded for the organizer; in list-only/employees-only it waits). Use a waiting message that matches the reason ('your ID is not on the organizer's list yet'). Collapse waiting rows from one device (second ID typed replaces the first). Show the organizer the typed ID and let 'Approve all' skip rows flagged as unknown ID.

gaps.title: Check-in forces a mobile-number confirmation and only accepts Indian 10-digit edits
gaps.scenario: An employee who joined with an ID only (mobile optional, none on file) opens check-in: the mobile row is empty and disabled, but the server rejects the submit unless confirmMobile is true, and the page keeps Submit asking to tick 'This mobile number is correct'. A participant from Dubai who edits their number gets 400 code bad-mobile 'The mobile number needs 10 digits.' because the server demands ^[6-9]\d{9}$ after stripping a leading 91 or 0. Typing 10 digits for a number stored as 91+10 is also recorded as an edit and overwrites the stored country-coded number with the 10-digit one.
gaps.recommendation: Require confirmMobile only when a number is on file (otherwise allow an empty/optional entry); accept any number the shared country-aware normaliser accepts (needs the country on this screen too); compare edits after normalising to E.164 so an unchanged number is not an edit; keep the stored digits country-coded.

gaps.title: Per-network join limits (200 per minute, 1,500 per day) will throttle a company event behind one office network, and the daily message is wrong
gaps.scenario: 1,000 staff join within a few minutes on the office Wi-Fi (one cf-connecting-ip): everyone beyond 200 in a minute gets 429 'It is busy right now. Please try again in a few minutes' and must press again by hand; at a 2,000-person site, everyone past 1,500 is locked out all day (UTC) with the same 'few minutes' text. Waiting requests are counted too. wrangler.toml sets neither JOIN_PER_IP_MINUTE nor JOIN_PER_IP_DAY (only DAILY_WRITE_BUDGET), so the code defaults are what production runs. The comment in the code says an office is far below the limit, which is not true for the product's main use.
gaps.recommendation: Raise the defaults and set them in [vars] for large games (for example scale with the game's cap), count per (network, game) instead of per network, do not count waiting/returning requests, differentiate the daily message ('your network has reached today's limit - ask your organizer'), and have the page retry a 429 busy automatically with jitter. Load-test with the 1,000-person plan behind one address.

gaps.title: Join phone check is much looser than the list check: typos become a different valid person and lock the phone
gaps.scenario: Participant types 98765 432101 (11 digits, one extra) or 12345 67890 (starts with 1) or 'office 98765 43210 ext 5' (letters dropped): digitsOf accepts any 10-15 digits, no Indian 6-9 rule, no '+91 must be followed by 10 digits'. In an open game the typo is a brand-new stranger and the phone gets a ticket at once; the person then tries the right number and gets 409 device-used 'This phone already holds a ticket in this engagement' - a dead end that only the organizer can clear (remove the wrong person). In a list game the typo just waits. The list side would have refused all of these with a reason.
gaps.recommendation: Use the same normaliser and messages as the list side at join. Show the cleaned number back for confirmation. For device-used, offer 'wrong number? start again' that releases a seat this device created moments ago (or let a participant who has not yet checked in replace their own identity).

gaps.title: Direct joiners' numbers are stored as typed (no country code); people list WhatsApp link and check-in comparisons break
gaps.scenario: Listed people carry 91xxxxxxxxxx in the sealed blob; an open-game joiner who typed 9876543210 is stored as 10 digits. viewOf/resendPerson then build https://wa.me/9876543210, which WhatsApp does not accept, so 'send link again' by WhatsApp fails for them; prize hand-over contact format differs by how the person joined.
gaps.recommendation: Store E.164 digits for everyone (see country fix); migrate nothing, just normalise at read for old rows (10 digits starting 6-9 means India).

gaps.title: Unbind / person / forget / mark take a mobile number only: ID-keyed participants cannot be found (misleading 404), and short foreign numbers cannot be typed
gaps.scenario: A listed employee known by ID alone loses their phone. Console 'Change of phone' (zc.js 764) asks for 'Their mobile number'; unbind hashes it and finds no seat because the seat is keyed by the ID hash, so the answer is 404 'That number has not joined this engagement.' The same applies to 'show/delete my data' and 'mark as host'. Only the People-list 'send link again' (resendPerson clears dev by the stored identity) works, which an organizer will not discover from the error.
gaps.recommendation: Let these routes accept empId or a person id as well; have the console search by name/ID/last 4 and call unbind with the seat; change the 404 text to say the person may be known by employee ID.

gaps.title: Places promised to listed people are not reserved in an open game
gaps.scenario: Cap 100, organizer lists 30 staff then shares an open link. Strangers fill 100 seats first; a listed employee then gets 409 'This engagement is full.' (no code). addPeople guards the cap with person rows, join guards it with participant rows only.
gaps.recommendation: In anyone-mode count listed-not-yet-joined persons against the cap for unlisted joiners (reserve places), or tell the organizer. Give the full answer a code and a plain next step.

gaps.title: A full Co-host or guest invite list sends invitees of an open game to the waiting room
gaps.scenario: Open game, Co-host link with the default limit of 100: the 101st person gets 409 invite-full and waits for the organizer even though the game is open to anyone. Guests (1-10 invites) hit this much sooner. Console copy says everyone with the link plays straight away.
gaps.recommendation: In an open game fall back to the organizer's list (no limit) instead of waiting; keep waiting only in list games. Or word the limit so it is clear it only counts people the Co-host personally lists.

gaps.title: Name is never required, never asked on a personal link, and the server gives the page no way to know whether a name is on file
gaps.scenario: Requirement: in ID-only mode the name is asked unless the organizer already supplied it for that ID, in which case it is used as is. Server side that part is right (listed name wins, typed name saved only when the list has none, worker.ts 1663) but join reply carries no name or flag, personal-link people never see a name box so a listed person with no name stays nameless, and the 'again' path ignores a typed name after first binding. The page cannot decide to show or hide the name box without leaking names by ID.
gaps.recommendation: Return { nameOnFile: true, firstName } in the join reply only after identity is established (not before), so the page can greet instead of asking; keep the name box visible but marked optional for people whose list entry has no name, including personal-link visitors; keep the listed name authoritative.

gaps.title: Mandatory versus optional is not exposed by the server; ID is only conditionally mandatory in mode both
gaps.scenario: Requirement: show red asterisk plus 'mandatory' on both fields when ID and mobile are both compulsory, '(optional)' on mobile for ID-only. Today info exposes only verify/employeesOnly (default shown as 'number' in info but 'mobile' in summary), and the page infers fields itself. In mode both without employees-only the ID is NOT mandatory for outsiders and is demanded only after consent for listed people with an ID, so the 'both compulsory' state exists only with employees-only on.
gaps.recommendation: Add one computed descriptor to info, e.g. join:{mobile:'required'|'optional'|'either-or-id'|'hidden', id:..., name:'optional', countryDefault:'IN'}, derived on the server from (verify, employeesOnly) so page and server cannot disagree; document the both/non-employees-only case as 'ID required if you are an employee'. Normalise 'number'/'mobile'.

gaps.title: Changing verify mode or employees-only after people are listed silently orphans them
gaps.scenario: List loaded in ID mode (people keyed by ID hash, many with no phone), then the organizer switches to mobile: the page asks only for a mobile, ID-keyed people without a phone can never match, and nothing warns. Switching employees-only off leaves closed=1 (line 2009 keeps e.closed) so the game stays list-only while the console says it is open.
gaps.recommendation: On a mode change with an existing list, warn with counts ('37 people are known by ID only') or re-key; when employees-only turns off, return whoCanJoin explicitly and make the console show it.

gaps.title: Leaving the game: wrong 'removed by the organizer' text, no way back after the start, list entry deleted before it
gaps.scenario: A participant leaves after the start (seat blocked, person status removed, removed_by self). Re-opening the link gives 403 removed 'You were removed from this game by the organizer.' Before the start leaving deletes their list entry, so in a list-only game coming back needs organizer approval.
gaps.recommendation: Return code left-by-self with its own text; keep the list entry (status left) before the start so returning is possible; allow the organizer to put the person back.

gaps.title: On a second phone the ID path says 'this link was already opened' and loops
gaps.scenario: Either mode: Asha joins by ID on phone A. On phone B she types her ID: the ID alias is adopted as a token, the seat is bound to A, and the 423 answer says 'This link was already opened on another phone ... type your own mobile number'. She never used a link, an ID-only person may have no mobile to type, and typing the ID again repeats the same answer.
gaps.recommendation: Use the other-phone text for typed ID/phone identities and name the fix ('ask your organizer to send your link again'). Distinguish token and typed identity in the code path.

gaps.title: Join answers are inconsistent: missing codes, a 403 for 'waiting', bad-id text, mode-both text
gaps.scenario: No code on: invalid mobile (400), nothing typed (400), refresh (400), game full (409), draft not open (403). Waiting is 403 (reads as 'forbidden'). bad-id says 'letters and numbers only' though . _ - / are allowed and 30 characters is the limit. Mode both with only an ID answers 'Enter a valid mobile number.' without naming the ID. Mode id open game and mode both employees-only use different texts for the same problem.
gaps.recommendation: Give every refusal a stable code, return 202 or 200 with waiting:true for the waiting room, align messages with the list-side texts, and state the 30-character and allowed-punctuation rule.

gaps.title: Join after the game has ended is not refused
gaps.scenario: The join route has no end-of-game check (endBoundMs is used by people/forget, not join). A late open or share of the link can create a seat and new personal data after the report; the waiting poll says 'lapsed / ask again' while join still answers 'waiting'. Verify with a test before changing.
gaps.recommendation: Refuse new joins after the end (code game-ended) and make the lapsed state's 'Ask again' text consistent.

gaps.title: Waiting screen can stay forever after the rows are erased
gaps.scenario: me?wid returns 404 state gone once personal data is erased; the page swallows the error and keeps polling the 'Please wait a moment' card.
gaps.recommendation: Handle state gone/404 in the page by clearing the saved wait and showing 'this game has ended'.

gaps.title: Last-10-digit identity collides across countries
gaps.scenario: Two people in different countries whose numbers share the last 10 digits are the same person ('same number twice = same participant'); the second gets other-phone 423.
gaps.recommendation: Hash the full E.164 digits for non-Indian numbers going forward (keep a last-10 alias for old rows) once country is captured.

gaps.title: Worker's join name cleaning is weaker than the people-list cleaning
gaps.scenario: The join strips only < > ` and cuts at 60; people.ts also removes control/invisible characters and a leading = + - @. A name typed as =HYPERLINK(...) or with a newline is stored raw and shows up in reports and CSV.
gaps.recommendation: Reuse the people.ts cleanName in join and check-in.

gaps.title: ID-miss counter moves before the consent and removed checks and on every retry
gaps.scenario: A reload, a double tap or the waiting-screen retry of the same wrong ID spends one of the 30 tries each time; a request without consent is counted too. Behind one network a few confused people exhaust the 30.
gaps.recommendation: Count only the first sight of a distinct (network, ID) per bucket, after consent.

gaps.title: A revoked Host or Co-host common link keeps working but credits the organizer
gaps.scenario: People using a revoked Host's link are still let in (open game) or queued with the organizer, and 'brought by' reports lose them.
gaps.recommendation: Return a clear 'this invitation link was withdrawn' for a revoked from= code, or record it.

gaps.title: Listed international numbers shorter than 10 digits can never be matched by typing
gaps.scenario: cleanPhone accepts 8-9 digit international numbers (small countries); digitsOf refuses anything under 10, so only the personal link works for them.
gaps.recommendation: Falls out of the shared normaliser fix.

gaps.title: Daily write accounting counts 3 per join but a join writes several more rows
gaps.scenario: spend(3) vs actual rows: usage, two rate-limit counters, seat, participant, person, consent_log plus index rows. On the free D1 cap (100,000 rows/day) the 80,000 'budget' may be reached after far fewer joins than the arithmetic suggests. This is an estimate from the code, not measured.
gaps.recommendation: Measure rows written per join in a load run (local.ts already counts) and set the per-join cost to the measured number.

analyses.findings:
SCOPE AND METHOD
Read-only analysis of C:\ct\test-sites\tambola (HEAD 274bde8 = 1.2.0 candidate; working tree has 5 unrelated uncommitted edits, z.js only changes check-in time-zone wording). Files read in full or in the relevant parts: apps/edge/src/people.ts, worker.ts (join 1558-1680, seats 1685-1707, invites 1906-1913, roster 1977-1997, settings 1998-2038, authOf 679-711), checkin.ts, winners.ts (digitsOf, confirm), rights.ts (leave), apps/web/public/z.js (participant page), zc.js (organizer console: step 2 audience, step 6 people/waiting), consent.js, common.js (TB.COUNTRIES), pages/functions/j/[[path]].ts, packages/beacon/src/config.ts (validateCfg, invites, verify), phone-runtime.ts (join). Nothing was run. "Public ticket id" claim: the /seats route is public and lists every pid after start+grace (worker.ts:1685-1706).

1. HOW THE ORGANIZER'S CHOICE BECOMES SERVER SETTINGS (zc.js:344-352, 1576)
"Who is this game for?" has six options; the server only stores closed (who can join), employeesOnly, verify (mobile|id|either|both) and invites{on,per,cats}.
| Console option | closed (list) | employeesOnly | invites | verify choices offered |
| 1 Only my employees | 1 | true | forced off | id (default), mobile, either, both |
| 2 Employees + friends and family | 1 | false | on | id, mobile, either, both |
| 3 A list I choose | 1 | false | off | mobile only |
| 4 A list + the people they invite | 1 | false | on | mobile only |
| 5 Anyone with the link | 0 | false | off | mobile only |
| 6 Anyone, employees confirm with ID | 0 | false | off | id or both only (either not offered) |
Consequence: through the console, guest invitations (common guest link) only ever exist together with a LIST-ONLY game (options 2 and 4). Games made through the API or the AI default to closed=0 (worker.ts:1406) and can combine invites with open entry.

2. WHAT THE PARTICIPANT PAGE SHOWS TODAY (z.js:87-116, 822-839)
Always first: two consent boxes (K4: "name and mobile number ... deleted within 24 hours", "I am 18 or older"); the Get my ticket button stays disabled until both are ticked. One generic heading "Join the engagement" and steps "Tick the boxes / Type your number / Get your ticket" (even for ID games).
| Mode | Fields shown, in order | Labels / hints |
| mobile | Mobile number, Name | "Your mobile number" (placeholder 98765 43210); "Your name (shown only to the organizer)" |
| id, employees-only | Employee ID, Name | hint "This game is for employees only."; NO mobile field at all |
| id, open | Employee ID, Mobile, Name | mobile labelled "No employee ID? Type your mobile number instead" + "Vendors, customers and families use their mobile number." |
| either | Mobile, "or", Employee ID, Name | hint "Give either one." (no employees-only note even when employeesOnly) |
| both, open | Mobile, Employee ID, Name | ID labelled "(employees only)" + "Not an employee? Leave this empty." |
| both, employees-only | Mobile, Employee ID, Name | ID hint "This game is for employees only." |
| mobile + employees-only | same as mobile | no employees-only note |
| personal link (/j/<token>) | no field, no name: "Your personal link is ready. Press the button" | |
| personal link already used on another phone (needPhone) | the mode's normal fields + name + banner "type your mobile number" | in employees-only ID mode only an ID box exists |
Nothing is marked mandatory or optional anywhere: no asterisk, no "(optional)", no "mandatory". No country selector exists (single text box, inputmode tel, autocomplete tel). The page does not use whoCanJoin/closed from /info, so a list-only game gives no advance notice that approval may be needed. A banner "You were invited by a colleague or family member. Join with your own mobile number" shows for ANY from= code (organizer, host, co-host, guest) and in every verify mode (z.js:106). There is no client-side validation of phone or ID before the call; everything is checked on the server after the consent ticks.

3. WHAT THE SERVER ENFORCES AT JOIN (worker.ts:1558-1680)
Order of checks: (a) token valid and not removed, else 404 link-gone; (b) typed phone, if any, must be 10-15 digits ("Enter a valid mobile number."); no Indian 6-9 prefix check; (c) employee ID must match [A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9._-/]{0,29} ("letters and numbers only"); (d) employees-only: id/both need an ID unless a token is used (need-id texts), either needs ID or mobile; (e) either-mode ID lookup: an ID that matches the list is treated exactly like a personal link (no phone check); (f) identity: ID-only people are keyed by hash(salt|emp|ID), everyone else by hash(salt|last 10 digits of the phone); (g) consent K4; (h) device id required; one device holds one ticket; (i) game full => flat 409 "This engagement is full." (no queue); (j) owner of the link is resolved from from=; (k) if the person is on no list: closed OR employee-ID-miss => waiting room; else join at once under the link owner, limited for Co-host (default 100) and level-1 guest (1-10); over limit => waiting under the Organizer with code invite-full.
Required by mode: mobile: phone. id: ID, or a phone if no ID. either: phone or ID. both: phone always; ID required only if employees-only or if the listed row has an ID (asked only after consent is ticked). Name is never required; mobile in ID-only games is never offered when employees-only.
Stored on join: participant{phone_hash, pii sealed {phone digits AS TYPED, name, empId}}, seat{seq,pid,ph,dev hash,jr,inv,cat,src,role}, person row (inviter, status joined), consent_log K4, kv counters keyed by hashed IP. Waiting: waiting{ph, sealed pii, via, inviter, chain, overlimit, status}. The typed number is stored un-normalized (could be 9876543210, 919876543210 or 09876543210), unlike list entries which are normalized with cleanPhone.

4. ROUTE BY ROUTE
| Route | Participant gives | Checked | Stored | Dead ends / contradictions |
| R1 Organizer common link z.html?e=ID (or &from=1900000000) | per mode (table 2) | open: nothing beyond format; list: must match a list entry else waiting; ID miss => waiting even in OPEN games | person under inviter "o" (unlimited) | message "This engagement is by invitation" is shown to a wrong-ID person in an open game; commonNote (zc.js:797) says "You do not need to approve anyone" for open games, untrue when IDs are used |
| R2 Host common link from=1.5e9+host id | same | Host key must exist and be unrevoked, else silently credited to the Organizer | person inviter h:xxxxxxx, unlimited | revoked/unknown code is silent, no error |
| R3 Co-host common link from=1e9+key7 | same | key checked; limit 100 (10-1000) counts personal-list AND common-link people | inviter c:xxxxxxx | the 101st gets "This invitation has already been used by 100 people ... most one person can invite" and goes to the Organizer; with the 500-request waiting cap a big open game via one Co-host spills; Co-host cannot add anyone in an employees-only ID game (gap 8) |
| R4 Level-1 guest common link from=<seat>&c=<kind> | same | organizer must have invites on; inviter seat exists, not removed, not itself invited (role seats allowed); category kept only if in organizer's list | seat.inv, seat.cat, person inviter s:N, limit 1-10 enforced inside the INSERT | in list games (every console-made invite game) the invitee WAITS and the inviter has no screen to approve; see gap 4 |
