5. USE-CASE MATRIX (owner's list)
| Use case | Today | Verdict |
| Employees only | Option 1; ID (default) or mobile/either/both; unlisted => waiting | works; no mandatory/optional marking; mobile not offered as optional; Co-host dead end |
| Employee ID only | keyed by ID hash; employees-only shows only the ID box | works; both-fields case misroutes (gap 7); mobile "(optional)" absent |
| Mobile number only | default; 10-15 digits | works for India-style numbers only; no country |
| ID and mobile (both) | phone required always, ID required if employees-only or listed with ID | works; no red asterisk/"mandatory" |
| ID or mobile (either) | ID hit = personal-link strength | works only if the list row has the field typed |
| Anyone / none of the above | Option 5, closed=0 | works; no invitations possible from console |
| Join via invite: personal or common link, guest invitations | see R4-R6 | personal path works; guest common link in list games is a dead end |
| Validated via invite | personal link (strong) vs typed match (weak) | as designed; UI never says which applies |
| Join without validation | Option 5 | works |
| Waiting room | list or ID-miss; organizer/host see all, Co-host sees own link, guest has API but no screen | partly works |
| Lists with names | list name wins, typed name silently ignored | works; page does not say so |
| Lists without names | name never captured for personal-link people; typed name saved otherwise | gap |
| Returning phone / second phone / wrong input / reload | see R6, R8, R11 | several dead ends |

6. KEY CONTRADICTIONS ALREADY VISIBLE IN THE CODE
- Ticket card for guests promises "Your guest joins with their own mobile number and gets their own ticket" while list games send that guest to a waiting room (z.js:467, 476 vs worker.ts:1665).
- Organizer help says a full game makes people wait (zc.js:225) but join answers a flat "This engagement is full." (worker.ts:1632).
- The organizer's own sentence for option 4 says invitations go "by WhatsApp" to people each guest adds (personal list), yet the same guests are given a common-link card.
- pub() reports verify "number" for the default while everything else uses "mobile" (worker.ts:104); harmless today because z.js maps unknown to mobile.

gaps.title: No country selection; join rejects national numbers shorter than 10 digits
gaps.scenario: A participant in Singapore (8 digits), Hong Kong (8), Israel/Spain/France (9) types the number as they always write it. Join runs digitsOf (10-15 digits) and answers 'Enter a valid mobile number.' There is no country box on z.js (single text input, line 89), z.html does not load common.js so TB.COUNTRIES (31 countries, no length data) is not even available, and the organizer-side cleanPhone (people.ts:62) and the guest 'My invites' form (z.js:529) apply different rules. The owner's first requirement (pick a country, default India, type the right national length) is not met anywhere on the participant path.
gaps.recommendation: Add a country dropdown (default India, +91) next to the number box on z.js, reuse the pay.js pattern (select + input autocomplete tel-national) and load the country list on z.html. Keep a small per-country table of allowed national lengths (min/max, e.g. IN 10, SG 8, FR 9, UK 10, US 10, AE 9) and validate in the page and again on the server. Send {cc, national} (or E.164) to join; the server builds one canonical E.164 string, strips trunk 0, and replaces the 10-15 digit rule in worker.ts digitsOf/phoneHash, people.ts cleanPhone, zc.js cleanPhone, z.js:529, checkin.ts:104 and winners.ts:28 with one shared function in packages/beacon (no length is a security matter, so accept the per-country range).

gaps.title: Mandatory / optional is never shown; ID-only games offer no optional mobile; nothing is marked
gaps.scenario: Employee ID only (employees-only): the page shows only the ID box and a name box, no mobile field, so 'mobile (optional)' does not exist. ID + mobile compulsory (both): both boxes look identical to optional ones; an employee can tap Get my ticket and learns only from a server message. No red asterisk, no 'mandatory', no '(optional)' exists in z.js. The name box is shown in every non-personal case and looks required but is not enforced.
gaps.recommendation: Rebuild joinWho as a field table driven by (verify, employeesOnly, personal link): mark each field with a small red * plus the word 'mandatory' in small type, or '(optional)'. Required fields per case: mobile mode => mobile mandatory; id+employees-only => ID mandatory, mobile (optional); id+open => ID or mobile (say which), either => one of the two (both marked 'one of these is mandatory'); both+employees-only => both mandatory; both+open => mobile mandatory, ID optional; none/anyone => mobile mandatory (or name only if the owner wants zero data). Add the same validation client-side so the error appears beside the field. Use the same wording on the personal-link screen when a number is still needed.

gaps.title: Name handling does not match the requirement: always asked, typed name silently dropped when the list has one, never captured for personal-link people without a listed name
gaps.scenario: List has 'Asha' for ID E1007. Asha types ID E1007 and her own spelling 'Asha K'; the page asks for a name regardless and the server keeps the list name (pii = pr.pii when a name exists), telling her nothing. Opposite case: list without names plus personal link: z.js:110 hides the name box for personal links, so the participant never gives a name, the check-in lets a blank name be 'confirmed' (z.js:725, checkin.ts:101-102) and the console shows 'No name'.
gaps.recommendation: Server: on join, if the matched list row has a name use it and return {nameKnown:true, name:first name}; if not, return code 'need-name' (400) so the page shows the name box only then; for personal links and for ID-first flows ask the name AFTER the ID/number is accepted (two-step), which also avoids leaking names to someone who only typed an ID. Page: hide the name box until the server asks; show 'Hello <name>' when the list supplied it. Make the check-in refuse a blank name or ask for it.

gaps.title: Guest common link in a list-only game ends in the waiting room with no approver screen, while the ticket page promises a ticket
gaps.scenario: Options 2 and 4 are list games with guest invitations. Asha (level-1 guest) shares the common-link card (invitation text: 'enter your mobile number and you get your own ticket'; line 476 'Your guest joins ... and gets their own ticket'). Her friend submits, worker.ts:1665 sends any unlisted person to wait() with chain ',s:N,<upline>,'. The friend is told 'Your request is with the person who invited you' (people.ts:598) but z.js has no waiting panel for guests (no /waiting call exists in z.js), the Organizer's waiting panel (zc.js:740) shows only 'Asking through the common link' and never which guest it belongs to, and nobody is notified.
gaps.recommendation: Decide the rule and make all three texts agree. Preferred: a valid guest link within the guest's quota counts as validation (join at once, still capped by per and by game size) while the organizer's own link and unlisted numbers keep waiting. Alternative: add an 'People waiting for you' card to z.js (GET /waiting?me=, POST /waiting/<id>) and show the inviter's label to the Organizer in zc.js. In either case change the invite card and WhatsApp text, and the Organizer help (zc.js:420, 425), to say what really happens in list games.

gaps.title: Level-1 guest API trusts the public ticket id with no device proof
gaps.scenario: After the first call the seat list is public: every pid is readable by every phone (worker.ts:1685-1706). callerOf accepts x-ct-pid / ?me= / body.me with only a seat lookup. Any participant can GET /api/z/<id>/people?me=<someone else's pid> and receive that guest's invitees: names, masked numbers, the personal link (token, usable to take the invitee's seat before they open it) and a wa.me link containing the FULL phone number (viewOf line 173). The same id lets them add junk to the list, list and admit/decline waiting requests in that guest's chain (people.ts:507-531), and call /invites.
gaps.recommendation: Require the ticket's device proof on every guest call exactly as checkin.ts deviceMatches does (send the phone's device id, compare the stored hash), and stop returning full numbers or tokens to guests unless the device matches; return a masked number and only generate the wa.me link client-side from data the guest just typed. Add tests that a second phone using a public pid gets 403.

gaps.title: Identity is the last 10 digits, so the same person typing a different format is not recognised for countries whose national number is not 10 digits
gaps.scenario: The organizer lists a French participant as +33 6 12 34 56 78. List hash uses the last 10 digits of 33612345678 = 3612345678. The participant opens the common link and types 06 12 34 56 78 (10 digits, 0612345678) or 6 12 34 56 78 (9 digits, rejected). The first does not match, so in a list game she waits for approval and the real list row stays 'invited' forever; the organizer later sees two people. Typing +33... works, but nothing tells her to. Indian and UK 10-digit numbers happen to survive, which hides the problem in tests. Also the join stores digits as typed, not normalised.
gaps.recommendation: Hash a canonical E.164 string (country calling code + national number without trunk 0) on both list and join paths, after the country picker gives the code. Migrate by recomputing ph for existing rows in the same game only if needed (rows are per game and short-lived). Add test cases for 8-, 9-, 10- and 11-digit national numbers entered with and without trunk zero.

gaps.title: Employee-ID modes: typing both ID and mobile, or the 'wrong' field for a list row, sends a legitimate listed person to the waiting room
gaps.scenario: verify=id (open or list): rows are keyed by the ID hash. The page shows ID plus 'No employee ID? Type your mobile number instead'; an employee fills both. typedGiven is true so idOnly is false, ph becomes the phone hash, personByPhone finds nothing, line 1615 sets idMiss, the employee waits for approval and one miss counts against the 30 per 10 minutes per network limit (worker.ts:388, 1616). Similar: verify=either with a list row that has only an ID, employee types their mobile => unlisted => waiting (or a second seat in an open game); verify changed to either/id AFTER a phone-only list was uploaded => nobody's ID matches.
gaps.recommendation: In id/either modes look the person up by ID hash first whenever an ID is typed (regardless of a typed phone), then by phone; store both keys (the idx/ pointer already exists for either mode) for every row that has both fields. Warn in the console when verify is changed and existing list rows lack the new field. Count a miss only when neither key matches.

gaps.title: A Co-host cannot add anyone in an employees-only ID or ID+mobile game
gaps.scenario: colsAllowed returns only 'mobile' for a Co-host, so the Co-host form has Name and Mobile only. addPeople rejects every such row with 'This game is for employees: the employee ID is missing.' (people.ts:289). The reason text lands in the 'look wrong' list with a Mobile input; nothing the Co-host can type fixes it.
gaps.recommendation: Give Co-hosts the same columns as the game's verify mode (id, both), or hide the Co-host add form and explain that this game's people are added by the Organizer or a Host. Load verify/employeesOnly into the Co-host console (GET /cohost does not return them today).

gaps.title: Winner prize confirmation rejects short numbers and keeps only the last 10 digits
gaps.scenario: A winner from Singapore (8 digits) or any 9-digit country presses Confirm and gets 'Please enter a valid mobile number.' (line 87); a UK winner's country code is thrown away by slice(-10). The prize hand-over record is the one place the owner says the mobile is genuinely needed.
gaps.recommendation: Use the same shared phone function as join (country + national), store E.164, accept per-country lengths, and show the country box on the Confirm your prize details card (z.js:317).

gaps.title: Check-in is India-only for mobile edits and makes ID-only people confirm an empty mobile
gaps.scenario: Check-in is mandatory for every game created after 2026-10-23. An edited mobile must match ^[6-9]\d{9}$ ('needs 10 digits'), so a UK or French participant cannot correct their number. An employee in an employees-only ID game has no mobile on file, yet the page shows a blank number and requires the box 'This mobile number is correct' (z.js:726-727; server line 88 demands confirmMobile). A blank name can also be confirmed.
gaps.recommendation: Skip the mobile confirmation when there is no number (show it as optional), accept the shared country-aware format when editing, and require a non-empty name or say it is optional.

gaps.title: Second phone / returning phone dead ends, especially for ID-only people and the used-link screen
gaps.scenario: (a) Personal link opened on a second phone: server returns link-used and the page asks to 'type your mobile number', but in employees-only ID games the form has no phone box, and the token is still sent, so typing an ID never helps (worker.ts:1598). (b) The organizer tool 'Let them move to a new phone' takes only a mobile number (zc.js:764, 1889; worker.ts:1750), but ID-only people are keyed by an ID hash, so it answers 'That number has not joined'; their row has no Send a new link button either because personRow offers it only after a WhatsApp send (zc.js:733). (c) Participant clears site data, switches from WhatsApp's browser to Chrome, or a typo'd number was bound on this phone: other-phone 423 or device-used 409 with only 'ask your organizer'.
gaps.recommendation: Offer the unbind by ticket number or by ID in the console (the API already accepts seat), add a 'Send a new link / move phone' action on every row including ID-only people (copy link when there is no phone), and show an ID box on the used-link screen when the game is ID-based. Add a one-line help on the join page for 'opened in WhatsApp then Chrome'.

gaps.title: Misleading texts on the join path
gaps.scenario: A wrong employee ID in an OPEN game gets 'This engagement is by invitation. Your request is with the organizer' (same for the 'type your number' step list for ID games, K4 text 'name and mobile number' in ID-only games, the 'invited by a colleague or family member' banner on organizer/host/co-host links, and the open-game note that no approval is ever needed).
gaps.recommendation: Use code-specific messages: 'That ID is not on the list. Check it, or ask the organizer to let you in' for an ID miss; make the steps, banner and K4 wording depend on verify mode and on the from= owner kind.

gaps.title: A full game refuses newcomers instead of queuing them, contrary to the organizer help
gaps.scenario: zc.js:225 tells organizers 'Nobody can join after the game is full: they wait in the waiting room until you make space.' The join answers 409 'This engagement is full.' before the waiting logic, for open and list games alike.
gaps.recommendation: Either send overflow requests to the waiting room (they use no place; admitting stops at the cap, which decideWaiting already enforces) or correct the help text.

gaps.title: Co-host / guest limits are shared with common-link joiners and the waiting cap is 500
gaps.scenario: A Co-host link posted in a 1,000-person WhatsApp group of an open game lets 100 in; the other 900 become 'invite-full' requests under the Organizer, the message blames the invitation, and request 501 onward is refused with 'Many people are waiting' (429).
gaps.recommendation: Count only personal-list entries against a Co-host's limit (or state the shared rule on the Co-host screen), raise or remove WAITING_MAX for approve-all flows, and rewrite the invite-full text.

gaps.title: Waiting requests are permanent per phone and 'Type it again' leaves ghosts
gaps.scenario: A declined phone gets 'declined' forever (addWaiting returns the old row, worker.ts:1655). 'Wrong number or ID? Type it again' (z.js:823) only resets the screen; the earlier request stays in the organizer's queue and may later be approved by mistake.
gaps.recommendation: Add a withdraw call used by the Type it again button, and let a declined person ask once more after the organizer re-opens or after a cool-down.

gaps.title: Join page does not announce approval rules or employees-only for mobile/either modes
gaps.scenario: /info already returns whoCanJoin, verify and employeesOnly, but z.js never reads whoCanJoin; employees-only with mobile or either shows no 'employees only' line (only id/both do). A stranger in a list game learns only after submitting.
gaps.recommendation: Show a short line before the fields: 'This game is for people on the organizer's list; others wait for approval' or 'Open to everyone'.

gaps.title: Guest 'My invites' form rejects valid international numbers
gaps.scenario: Client check: name at least 2 characters and phone at least 10 digits. A guest adding a +65 colleague with 8 digits is told 'Please type their mobile number' although people.ts cleanPhone would accept it with a plus sign.
gaps.recommendation: Use the shared country-aware validator; allow a one-letter or missing name only if the owner wants names optional.

gaps.title: Per-network limits can block a real office or the 1,000-person test
gaps.scenario: JOIN_PER_IP_MINUTE 200 and JOIN_PER_IP_DAY 1500 apply to every new seat or waiting request; ID misses 30 per 10 minutes. 1,000 staff behind one office address or a test rig on one cloud IP will hit 429 'It is busy' for a third of them.
gaps.recommendation: Raise the env overrides for the test, and for production key the limit on network+game with a higher ceiling or exempt personal-link and listed joins.

gaps.title: Roster enumeration oracles on join and guest add
gaps.scenario: In both mode the need-id answer appears only for a number that is on the list with an ID, and the comment says the consent order prevents guessing, but ticking two boxes is trivial. A guest's add answers 'duplicate' or 'This person was removed' for numbers on other people's lists (people.ts:316).
gaps.recommendation: Return one neutral outcome for 'not accepted' and let the organizer's waiting room deal with it; give guests only counts, not per-number reasons.

gaps.title: Invite categories are weakly connected
gaps.scenario: The category is chosen by the inviter's chip and travels as c= only on the common link; personal-list invites carry none; the invitee never sees it. I found no participant-facing use; it is returned by the participants route (line 1880).
gaps.recommendation: Add a category choice to My invites rows or drop the feature from the guest card.

gaps.title: Personal links for ID-only people are not reachable in the console
gaps.scenario: personRow builds buttons from waLink; without a phone there is none, so only the CSV export holds the link.
gaps.recommendation: Add 'Copy personal link' for every non-removed row.

gaps.title: Leave then rejoin in a list game drops the list line
gaps.scenario: A person who leaves before the start is deleted from the list (personal link dead); returning means waiting for approval again. After the start the page tells a self-leaver 'removed by the organizer'.
gaps.recommendation: Keep the line as 'left' before the start, and use wording for self-leave.

gaps.title: Unknown or revoked Host/Co-host code is silently credited to the Organizer
gaps.scenario: A retired Co-host's link keeps working as the organizer's link with no sign to the person or the Organizer.
gaps.recommendation: Record via='revoked-link' so the Organizer's waiting panel and reports show it.

gaps.title: Verify default token mismatch ('number' vs 'mobile')
gaps.scenario: pub() emits verify 'number' for a default game; zc.js vmode() compares with 'mobile' and falls back to it only when the summary is loaded.
gaps.recommendation: Emit 'mobile'.

analyses.findings:
SCOPE AND METHOD
Read-only analysis of the working tree (release candidate 1.2.0; the only uncommitted edit to z.js is the check-in time-zone text, unrelated to phones). Nothing was run. The country table in "data" is written from ITU/libphonenumber knowledge, NOT machine-verified: ranges are deliberately wide where unsure (list at the end) and must be proven by a table-driven test (see section F).

A. WHAT THE CODE DOES TODAY

A1. The participant join page (apps/web/public/z.js lines 87-95, 103-115, 827-839)
- ONE free-text box id="ph", label "Your mobile number" (or "No employee ID? Type your mobile number instead" when the game asks for ID first), inputmode="tel", autocomplete="tel", placeholder "98765 43210" (an Indian example, whatever country the person is in).
- No country control, no hint about country codes, no "(optional)" / "mandatory" marker, no client-side check at all. The raw string goes straight to POST /api/z/<id>/join as `phone` (packages/beacon/src/phone-runtime.ts:291-293).
- Server refusal text is always the same: "Enter a valid mobile number." (worker.ts:1569, 1584). It never says why, never mentions a country code.

A2. How the server reads a typed number on JOIN (apps/edge/src/worker.ts)
- digitsOf (line 1489): drop every non-digit, accept 10 to 15 digits, nothing else. cleanPhone is NOT called on join.
- phoneHash (1490-1494): sha256(PHONE_SALT | LAST 10 DIGITS). Same formula as people.ts:48 phoneHashOf. This is the "one ticket per phone" key (unique index participant_phone / person_phone / waiting_phone / seat.ph).
- Stored in the sealed record: the digits exactly as typed (1582, 1669): "9876543210" for a plain Indian join, "919876543210" if +91 was typed, "07911123456" for a UK national format. When the person is on a list, the LIST's sealed digits win (1663).
- Roster add, "forget/person", "unbind", "mark role" use the same digitsOf/phoneHash (1726, 1750, 1896, 1987).

A3. How the server reads a number on the ORGANIZER LISTS (people.ts cleanPhone 62-77)
- Allowed characters only digits, space + - ( ) . /
- Typed with + or 00 and not 91: international, 8 to 15 digits, kept as typed, no country-code check, no per-country length (so "+99999999" passes).
- Otherwise India is assumed: leading 00 dropped; an 11-digit number starting 0 loses the 0; 10 digits must start 6-9 ("An Indian mobile number starts with 6, 7, 8 or 9."); 12 digits starting 91 ok; any other number starting 91 -> "After +91 there must be 10 digits."; 11-15 digits accepted as they are (assumed to contain a country code); else "too short / too long for a mobile number".
- Result digits always carry 91 for Indians. Hash = last 10 digits of that, so it equals the join hash.
- The console (zc.js 592-600 cleanPhone, 622-638 cleanBatch) has a near copy and sends "+"+digits to /people (zc.js:713).

A4. Where a number is hashed / stored / shown / sent
| Place | Code | What is kept | Note |
| Join (self, waiting room, roster) | worker.ts:1489-1494, 1582, 1669; people.ts:604 addWaiting | digits as typed (no country code added) | hash = last 10 |
| Organizer list, My invites | people.ts:297-307 | cleanPhone digits (91+10 for India) | hash = last 10 |
| Personal link /j/<token> | worker.ts:1560-1566, 1663 | list's sealed digits | no number typed |
| Link used on another phone (needPhone) | worker.ts:1598 | typed digits again | same box |
| Check-in edit | checkin.ts:103-107; z.js:726 | national 10 digits, Indian only | error "The mobile number needs 10 digits." |
| Prize confirm (winner) | winners.ts:28, 85-91 | LAST 10 DIGITS ONLY | country code lost |
| Organizer contact | worker.ts:1841, 1857, 1869 | last 10 digits only | re-read by people.ts:465 as Indian |
| Host mobile | worker.ts:1118-1125; hostsetup.ts:101-107 | cleanPhone digits | ok |
| Co-host mobile | worker.ts:1180-1189 | digits, leading zeros dropped, no country code, 10-15 | not cleanPhone |
| Masked on screen | people.ts:78, checkin.ts:82, hostsetup.ts:30, worker.ts:1167/1191, rights.ts:115/122 | "******"+last 4 (or "ending xx") | no country shown |
| Sent to someone (wa.me) | people.ts:108/358/452, worker.ts:637/1134/1158, zc.js:586-587/643/1789 | stored digits | needs full country-code digits |
| Reports / CSV | report-layout.ts:38 mob(); people.ts:374 | raw digits; only exact 10-digit ones grouped | 12-15 digit numbers shown bare |
| Waiting-room restore | z.js:136-142, 160 | typed text kept on the phone | no country kept |

A5. What typed text does today (join vs list)
| Typed | JOIN | LIST |
| 98765 43210 | ok, stored 9876543210 | ok, stored 919876543210 |
| 1234567890 or 0000000000 | ACCEPTED (no format check) | refused (must start 6-9) |
| 9876543210abc | ACCEPTED (letters dropped) | refused ("only digits") |
| +65 9123 4567 | ok (10 digits) | ok |
| 9123 4567 (Singapore, no code) | refused "Enter a valid mobile number." | refused "After +91 there must be 10 digits." (it starts 91) |
| 06 12 34 56 78 (France, national) | accepted, hash of 0612345678 -> does NOT match a listed "+33 6 12 34 56 78" (hash 3612345678) -> goes to waiting room / outsider | refused (not 6-9 start) |
| 07911 123456 (UK, national) | accepted, hash 7911123456 matches listed +44 number | becomes +91 7911123456 (WRONG country, stored 917911123456) |
| 415 555 2671 (US) | accepted, matches a listed +1 number | refused |
| 702 555 0123 (US, Las Vegas) | accepted | becomes +91 702 555 0123 (WRONG country) |
| 0151 12345678 (Germany, national) | accepted | stored as 015112345678 (leading 0 kept; wa.me link broken) |
| +298 123456 (Faroe, 9 digits) | refused (<10 digits) | accepted (>=8) |
| +971 50 123 4567 | ok | ok |

Observed consequences: (1) the join page and the list page disagree on what a number is; (2) every non-Indian number typed without "+" is guessed to be Indian on lists; (3) the hash saves identity for national numbers of 10+ digits only; (4) the contact digits kept for winners/organizers are mangled for foreign numbers (winners.ts, worker.ts:1841/1857).

B. COMPARISON WITH THE OWNER'S REQUIREMENTS
- Pick a country (default India): NOT MET. There is no control anywhere in the shipped player or console pages. A legacy, not-shipped page (play.js:84, 32; docs/dev/02-FILE-MAP.md:220) and the payment page (pay.js:68, common.js:96-102 TB.COUNTRIES, only 31 countries, no flag, no search, no lengths) show the house pattern, but z.html and zc.html do not even load common.js.
- Right length per country (8, 9, 10, 11, 12 digits): NOT MET. Join accepts only 10-15 digits in total with no per-country rule; lists accept anything 8-15 after "+".
- Optional/mandatory marks: NOT MET on the phone field (no asterisk, no word "mandatory", no "(optional)"); covered by the other focus areas but the new control must carry the marker.
- Minimum capture: stored digits are inconsistent (see A4), which is the opposite of "keep only what the game needs".

C. PROPOSED DESIGN

C1. One source of truth
- New packages/shared/src/dial.ts holding the table in "data", plus parseMobile(raw, ccIso?) -> {ok, cc, national, e164digits} | {ok:false, why}, maskMobile(), formatIntl(). No libphonenumber-js (packages/shared/src/phone.ts uses it, but only the legacy server mode imports it; the pages run under script-src 'self' and a free Worker, so a ~10 KB table beats a hundreds-of-KB metadata file).
- Built for browsers like zgame.js (package.json "build:zgame" pattern) into apps/web/public/dial.js, and imported directly by the Worker (worker.ts:35 already imports from packages/shared/src). Wire it in: pages/build.mjs FILES (line 8), zsw.js FILES (line 11), script tags in z.html and zc.html, and the file list in test ai-mail.test.ts:114. A file missing from pages/build.mjs FILES is silently NOT shipped.

C2. The control on the join page (and My invites, prize confirm, check-in edit, Host/Co-host/list forms)
- Compound field: [flag +dial v] [national number input]. Label "Your mobile number" + marker: mandatory = small red asterisk + the word "mandatory" in small type; optional = "(optional)" in brackets (employee-ID-only and ID-or-mobile modes decided by verifyOf).
- Left part is a button (aria-haspopup="dialog") showing flag emoji + "+91". It opens a full-width bottom sheet with a search box (type=search, inputmode=search, autocomplete=off) focused at once, so the phone keyboard is already up. List: India first (pinned), then A-Z. Each row >= 44 px: flag (aria-hidden) + English name + "+dial" on the right. Typing filters by name words, dial code ("65", "+65", "971") and ISO2 ("sg"), ignoring accents. Esc / back closes; selection returns focus to the number box. role=dialog, aria-modal, listbox/option, aria-selected.
- Flags are computed from ISO2 (regional-indicator code points). Windows desktop Chrome/Edge draws letters instead of flags, so name + dial code must always be in the row text; the flag is decoration only.
- Default country India. Remember the chosen country for that game in localStorage (country is not personal data) so a reload or "type it again" does not reset it. Optional later: organizer setting "numbers without a country code are read as" (the legacy console.js:495 had exactly this) that also pre-selects the country on the join page (legacy play.js:65 info.defaultCountry).
- Number box: inputmode="tel", autocomplete="tel-national" (plain "tel" autofills "+91 98765 43210" and would double the code), no maxlength under 20 characters (Austria allows 13 digits; the check-in box today has maxlength 14 which cuts "+971 50 123 4567").
- Placeholder/hint from the table, no invented examples: "10 digits" / "8 or 9 digits"; for India keep "98765 43210".
- Live preview under the box once there are digits: "We will use +65 9123 4567" (country code, then plain grouping). This is what catches a UK person who left India selected.
- Validate on blur and on submit, not on each keystroke.

C3. Parsing rules (identical in browser and Worker)
1. Keep only digits; reject letters/emoji with "A number has only digits. Please remove the letters."
2. Pasted/autofilled text starting with + or 00: read the longest matching dial code (3, 2, 1 digits), set the selector, move the rest to the number box. Shared dial codes map to a primary country: 1 US, 7 RU, 39 IT, 44 GB, 47 NO, 61 AU, 212 MA, 262 RE, 358 FI, 590 GP, 599 CW (validation does not depend on which, ranges are the same). Unknown code: "We do not know the code +xxx. Pick your country from the list."
3. If the box starts with the selected country's own code and the remainder fits the range, drop it and say so ("We moved +65 to the country box").
4. Trunk prefix: strip a leading trunk (usually 0; 8 for RU/KZ/BY/UZ/TM/LT; 06 for HU) or "(0)" ONLY when the country has a trunk in the table AND the remainder lies inside [minNational, maxNational]. Countries with no trunk entry never lose a leading 0 (Cote d'Ivoire, Benin, Italy, Gabon, Congo keep it as part of the number).
5. Length check against the country's range. Messages name the country and the count, e.g. "A mobile number in Singapore has 8 digits after +65. You typed 7." or "...has 9 to 10 digits...". Keep the India sentence "An Indian mobile number starts with 6, 7, 8 or 9." for IN only (existing tests depend on it).
6. Empty box = nothing sent, ever. Never compose a lone "+91" (the server would read "91" as a typed number and refuse an OPTIONAL field).

C4. What the client sends and how the server stays compatible
- Send phone = "+" + cc + national digits (no trunk, no spaces) and a new optional `cc` = ISO2. Join (worker.ts:1568) keeps working: digitsOf strips the "+", and the hash (last 10 digits) is exactly what the same person gets from a list entry in any format, because both sides now contain the country code. Verified on paper for IN, GB, DE, FR, SG, BR, MX, AR.
- Server changes (all backward compatible):
  a) digitsOf minimum 10 -> 7 only when a valid `cc` is sent and the national length is inside that country's range; without `cc` (old cached page, hand-made request) behave exactly as today. Needed because cc+national is under 10 digits for about 20 territories (Faroe, Greenland, Andorra, Cook Islands, Niue, Tokelau, St Helena, Tuvalu, Tonga, Wallis, St Pierre, New Caledonia, Norfolk, Falkland, Ascension...). cleanPhone's international minimum 8 -> 7 for the same reason.
  b) store FULL digits (country code + national) on every path; for an old client that typed 10 plain Indian digits add 91 so the stored form is the same as the list's.
  c) cleanPhone(raw, defaultCc = "91"): India behaviour unchanged for the default; a "+" number is checked against the table (known code, per-country length). tools/load-tests/sigma-steps.mjs:107-108, people.test.ts:44-48 and param-people.test.ts:12-37 must stay green (10 digits starting 1-5 rejected for the default).
  d) winners.ts:28/85-91, checkin.ts:103-104, worker.ts:1180-1182 and 1840-1869 use the same parse and keep full digits; "changed" compares last 10 only to avoid false edits.
  e) masks: "+<cc> ****" plus last 3 (last 4 only when the national part has 8+ digits); show the country code everywhere an organizer sees a number.
- Do NOT change the hash in 1.2.0. person.ph / seat.ph / participant.phone_hash exist in live games and roster re-use depends on "one hash in every game" (people.ts:47-48). Phase 2 option: for non-India numbers hash the full digits and look up both new and legacy hash.

C5. One ticket per phone, same national number in two countries
- Because the hash is the last 10 digits, two different people collide when cc+national share their last 10 digits. Real shapes: Brazil 11 9xxxx-xxxx and 21 9xxxx-xxxx (same subscriber, different area code: both end ...1912345678); an Indian 10-digit number starting 7/8/9 and a UK/US/NG/PH/NP number with the same ten digits; countries with 11+ digit national numbers (BR, CN, ID, AT, DE) lose their first digits. Probability in one game is tiny, but the effect is confusing: the second person gets "ticket opened in a different browser" (423) or, if the first listed person has not opened their link, can take that ticket.
- The same number typed with and without the trunk 0 is safe today only when the national part has 10+ digits; for 8-9 digit countries (FR, ES, PT, NL, PL, AU, SG, HK) it works only when the country code is sent, which the new control guarantees. A page cached from 1.1.8 (zsw.js) talking to a 1.2.0 server will still mismatch for those countries, hence the "keep old behaviour when `cc` is absent" rule.
- A person who leaves India selected and types a foreign number that happens to look Indian (UK 7xxx, US 6xx-9xx) is accepted as +91. Identity still matches a listed +44/+1 person (same last 10), but the contact digits are wrong; the live preview and a country field on the prize-confirm form are the mitigation.

D. PER-USE-CASE NOTES FOR THE CONTROL
- Employee ID only: mobile marked "(optional)", empty = not sent; if filled it must pass the country rule (the server already refuses a typed-but-invalid number, worker.ts:1569).
- ID + mobile both compulsory: red asterisk + "mandatory" on both.
- Mobile only / anyone can join: mobile mandatory (it is the ticket key).
- Personal link: no number field unless the server answers link-used/needPhone (z.js:171); then the selector shows.
- Common link, guest invitation, waiting room, "type it again" (z.js:100, 823), reload (z.js:136-142): the saved waiting state must hold country + national (or the composed +digits); today it holds only the typed text, so after admission doJoin() (z.js:152, 160) would re-send national digits without the code.
- Returning phone / second phone: unchanged; device lock is separate from the number.

E. TESTS TO ADD
Table-driven over all 244 rows: a generated number of minNational and of maxNational digits passes, min-1 and max+1 fail, trunk strip works only where a trunk exists, "+cc" paste picks the right country; cross-format hash equality (list "+65 9123 4567" == join "+65 91234567" == old-client "6591234567"); India regressions; Cote d'Ivoire keeps its leading 0; "+298..." can join; prize confirm and check-in keep full digits.

F. DATA NOTES (field "data")
- 244 rows = every ISO 3166-1 territory that has a dial code, minus AQ, BV, GS, HM, PN, TF, UM, plus XK (Kosovo) and AC (Ascension). India first, then A-Z by English name. Ranges are MOBILE national lengths, not landline.
- Verify before trusting: add a devDependency test that, for each iso2, checks libphonenumber-js `getExampleNumber(iso2, examples)` (from "libphonenumber-js/mobile/examples") has a nationalNumber length inside [minNational, maxNational] and `getCountryCallingCode(iso2)` equals dial. libphonenumber-js is already in bun.lock via packages/shared.
- Deliberately wide (unsure or genuinely variable): AD, AT, AX/FI, BJ, BW, CI, GW, ID, IS, KI, KP, LA, LR, LU, LY, MM, NA, NU, SH, SM, SO, SE, SY, TK, TO, TV, VA, VU, WS, ZW. Argentina 10-11 (leading 9 after +54), Mexico 10-11 (legacy 1 after +52), Benin and Cote d'Ivoire 8-10 (moved to 10-digit plans in 2024 / 2021).
- Shared dial codes: 1 (25 entries: US, CA + 23 Caribbean/Pacific), 7 (RU, KZ), 39 (IT, VA), 44 (GB, GG, JE, IM), 47 (NO, SJ), 61 (AU, CX, CC), 212 (MA, EH), 262 (RE, YT), 358 (FI, AX), 590 (GP, BL, MF), 599 (CW, BQ). A dial code alone therefore cannot name the country; the selector stores ISO2.
- trunk key present only where the national format really uses it; absent means "never strip".
- Names with accents are written in UTF-8; fold accents when sorting/filtering.

G. OTHER RISKS NOTED
- CSV export writes bare digits (people.ts:374); spreadsheets turn 12-15 digit numbers into 9.19877E+11. Write "+<cc> <national>" as text.
- A new script cannot come from a CDN (script-src 'self' in pages/build.mjs CSP), so the table must ship as our own file.
- Edits must not break the existing 1.1.8 phones during rollout; the join route must stay tolerant (A2) until old pages are gone.

gaps.title: No country selector or country-code guidance anywhere on the participant join page
gaps.scenario: A participant in Singapore, UAE or the UK opens the game link. The only field is one text box with the Indian example 98765 43210 and no way to choose a country. Typing the local number 9123 4567 is refused with the bare text 'Enter a valid mobile number.' and nobody tells them to add +65.
gaps.recommendation: Add the compound control from section C2 (flag + dial code button opening a searchable bottom sheet, India default, national-number box, live 'We will use +65 9123 4567' preview, mandatory/optional marker). Send phone as '+<cc><national>' plus cc=ISO2; empty box sends nothing. Reuse the same control in My invites, prize confirm, check-in edit and the console forms.

gaps.title: Prize confirmation keeps only the LAST 10 digits, losing the country code and part of longer numbers
gaps.scenario: A winner in the UAE confirms +971 50 123 4567. winners.ts digitsOf returns slice(-10) = 1501234567, which is stored as the number the prize goes to; the organizer sees a number that cannot be called. German/Austrian/Brazilian/Indonesian numbers lose leading digits too, and an Indian winner's correct 919876543210 is overwritten by 9876543210. Numbers whose country code plus national part are under 10 digits are refused outright.
gaps.recommendation: Use the shared parser, store full country-code digits, compare 'changed' on last 10 only, lower the minimum to 7 when a valid country is given, and show the formatted +cc number in the confirm form with a country selector.

gaps.title: Join route rejects valid foreign numbers: minimum 10 digits and no per-country rule
gaps.scenario: Faroe, Greenland, Andorra, Tuvalu, Tonga and about 15 other territories have cc plus national shorter than 10 digits, so they can be put on a list (cleanPhone accepts 8+) but can never join (digitsOf returns null). Everyone with an 8-9 digit national number who types it without +cc is refused with no explanation.
gaps.recommendation: Accept 7-15 digits when a valid cc is sent and the national length is inside that country's range; keep the 10-digit rule only when cc is absent (old pages). Return a country-specific message instead of the generic one. Align cleanPhone's international minimum with 7.

gaps.title: Join does no format validation: junk and letters are accepted, list route is strict
gaps.scenario: A participant types 1234567890, 0000000000 or 9876543210abc into an open game and gets a ticket (letters are silently dropped); the same text is refused when an organizer adds it to a list. A single mistyped digit is caught only by length, so a wrong 10-digit number is stored and the prize cannot be handed over.
gaps.recommendation: Run the shared parser on join (client and server) so both routes agree: letters refused, per-country length, India 6-9 start only for IN. Keep tolerance for requests without cc.

gaps.title: Stored participant number format is inconsistent (typed digits vs country-code digits)
gaps.scenario: A self-joiner who types 98765 43210 is stored as 9876543210, one who types +91... as 919876543210, a UK joiner as 07911123456, while the organizer's list stores 91 plus ten digits. Reports, prize lists and any WhatsApp or phone hand-over then show or use numbers without a country code, or with a leading trunk 0.
gaps.recommendation: Always store full E.164 digits (country code + national, no trunk 0) on every path; for an old client that typed plain 10 Indian digits prepend 91. Migrate nothing: display code can tolerate old rows.

gaps.title: List parsing silently reads foreign numbers typed without + as Indian
gaps.scenario: An organizer pastes a UK list with 07911 123456: the trunk 0 is dropped and 7911123456 passes the Indian 6-9 test, so it is saved as +91 7911123456. A US 702 555 0123 does the same; US numbers starting 2-5 are refused. The personal-link WhatsApp button then opens a chat with a stranger in India. German 0151 12345678 is kept with its leading 0 and the wa.me link is broken. The console copy (zc.js:592-600) behaves the same.
gaps.recommendation: Add cleanPhone(raw, defaultCc='91') and an organizer setting 'numbers without a country code are read as' (default India) in the list step and the My-people forms; show the resulting +cc number after adding; apply the table so 07911... under GB becomes +44 7911 123456.

gaps.title: Check-in refuses any non-Indian mobile and the box is too short for an international number
gaps.scenario: In a game with check-in, an overseas participant who needs to correct the number types +971 50 123 4567; the box cuts it at 14 characters and the server answers 'The mobile number needs 10 digits.' because only /^[6-9]\d{9}$/ is allowed. An Indian participant who retypes the same number is also treated as an edit because the stored value is 91+10 while the typed value has 91 stripped, and the stored number is rewritten without the country code.
gaps.recommendation: Use the shared parser and the country selector in the check-in edit, raise maxlength to at least 20, compare on last 10 for 'edited', keep full digits.

gaps.title: Organizer contact number is cut to 10 digits and then re-read as Indian
gaps.scenario: An organizer in Singapore publishes with +65 9123 4567. The server keeps only 6591234567 (slice(-10)); myOwnSeat later runs cleanPhone on it, sees 10 digits starting 6 and builds +91 6591234567, so the organizer's own play link goes to a wrong person on WhatsApp. A +971 organizer's 1501234567 is rejected as 'not Indian' and the seat cannot be made.
gaps.recommendation: Store the full digits in contact/<eid> and read them back through the same parser; drop slice(-10) on lines 1841, 1857 and 1869.

gaps.title: Waiting-room and 'type it again' state keep only the typed text, not the country
gaps.scenario: A Singapore participant waits for approval, reloads, then is admitted: doJoin() re-sends the saved text 9123 4567 without +65 and the join is refused or matches the wrong person. The waiting screen shows 'You asked with 9123 4567' with no country.
gaps.recommendation: Save and restore {cc, national} (or the composed +digits) in the saved wait record and in J; repopulate the selector when the person presses 'Type it again'; remember the country per game in localStorage.

gaps.title: Optional-mobile trap: a pre-selected country must never produce a lone '+91'
gaps.scenario: With employee-ID-only (mobile optional) the new control defaults to India. If the client composes '+' + cc + national when the box is empty, the server sees digits '91', treats a number as typed and answers 'Enter a valid mobile number', blocking a person who legitimately left it empty.
gaps.recommendation: Compose the phone only when the national box has digits; otherwise send no phone and no cc. Add a test for ID-only and ID-or-mobile modes with an empty box.

gaps.title: Hash is the last 10 digits: different people can collide, and 8-9 digit countries need the country code to match
gaps.scenario: Brazil 11 91234-5678 and 21 91234-5678 hash identically; an Indian 7/8/9xxxxxxxxx number and a UK/US/NG/PH number with the same ten digits collide; a page cached from 1.1.8 sending the French national 0612345678 never matches a listed +33 6 12 34 56 78 (3612345678). The second colliding person gets a confusing 'opened in a different browser' error, or takes a listed person's unopened ticket.
gaps.recommendation: Do not change the hash in 1.2.0 (live data, roster re-use). Require cc+national from the new client (fixes the 8-9 digit case), keep old behaviour only when cc is absent, and plan a phase 2 that hashes full digits for non-India numbers with dual lookup (new and legacy hash).

gaps.title: Server accepts any '+' number of 8-15 digits: no country-code check, generic error text
gaps.scenario: '+99999999' or '+12345678' is accepted as a valid mobile number; a typo in the country code is not noticed; errors say only 'too short/too long for a mobile number' without naming the country or the expected digits.
gaps.recommendation: Check the code against the table and the length against the country's range; messages like 'A mobile number in Singapore has 8 digits after +65. You typed 7.'

gaps.title: Console lists, Host, Co-host and My invites forms assume Indian numbers
gaps.scenario: A Host in Singapore types 9123 4567: the console refuses it because fewer than 10 digits (zc.js:1780); the Co-host server route stores raw digits without country code (worker.ts:1180-1182) and the co-host's own play link is later built as Indian; a guest abroad inviting a friend is stopped by the <10 digit test (z.js:529); list uploads of 8-9 digit local numbers fail (zc.js:599, looksPhone accepts 8 digits at 1641 but cleanPhone does not).
gaps.recommendation: Put the same selector and parser behind every phone field (zc.js hostphone, cohostphone, gphone, pdph, ubph, myph, setupmobile; z.js mi-phone, cfph, ckmob) and route /api/org/cohost through cleanPhone.

gaps.title: Rollout compatibility: pages cached by the service worker still send raw national digits
gaps.scenario: During and after the 1.2.0 deploy, phones holding the 1.1.8 z.js (zsw.js cache) join against the new server. If the server tightens join validation for everybody, those phones start failing or, for 8-9 digit countries, mismatching.
gaps.recommendation: Tighten only when the request carries cc; keep today's tolerant path otherwise. Add dial.js to pages/build.mjs FILES (line 8), zsw.js FILES (line 11), z.html/zc.html script tags and ai-mail.test.ts:114 so the new file is shipped and cached.

gaps.title: Autofill and paste put the country code in the number box
gaps.scenario: autocomplete='tel' fills '+91 98765 43210' into the field; with a separate country control this doubles the code or fails the length check. People also paste '+44 (0)7911 123456'.
gaps.recommendation: Use autocomplete='tel-national' on the number box; on input detect leading + / 00, select the longest matching dial code, drop '(0)' and move the rest to the box; strip the selected country's own code when the remainder fits.

gaps.title: Trunk-prefix rule must be per country, not 'drop a leading 0'
gaps.scenario: Blindly dropping a leading 0 breaks Cote d'Ivoire and Benin (the 0 is part of the 10-digit number), Italy, Gabon and Congo; not dropping it breaks UK, German, Australian, Russian (8) and Hungarian (06) national formats.
gaps.recommendation: Use the table's optional trunk field; strip only when present and when the remainder is inside [minNational, maxNational].

gaps.title: Masked numbers show no country and can reveal the whole number for tiny countries
gaps.scenario: '******'+last 4 hides nothing for Niue, Tokelau and St Helena (national numbers of 4-5 digits) and nothing tells an organizer whether a number is +91 or +65. Data-rights text 'ending xx' has the same gap.
gaps.recommendation: Mask as '+<cc> ****' plus last 3 (last 4 only when the national part has 8+ digits); use one maskMobile in people.ts:78, checkin.ts:82, hostsetup.ts:30, worker.ts:1167/1191, rights.ts:115/122.

gaps.title: Organizer views, reports and CSV print bare digits
gaps.scenario: report-layout mob() groups only exact 10-digit numbers, so 12-15 digit numbers appear as one long string; the people CSV writes bare digits that spreadsheets turn into 9.19877E+11, hiding the country code.
gaps.recommendation: Show '+<cc> <national>' as text everywhere (formatIntl); in CSV write the + form so spreadsheets keep it as text.

gaps.title: Flag emoji do not render on Windows desktop browsers
gaps.scenario: Employees on Windows laptops see two letters instead of a flag; a design that relies on the flag alone would be unreadable.
gaps.recommendation: Always render the English name and +dial in the list and the button text; mark the flag aria-hidden and treat it as decoration.

gaps.title: Existing country list is too small and not loaded on the live pages
gaps.scenario: TB.COUNTRIES holds 31 countries (no flags, no search, no lengths) and is only used by payment pages; z.html and zc.html do not load common.js, so the join page cannot reuse it.
gaps.recommendation: Replace with the 244-row table in a new shared file loaded by z.html and zc.html; keep TB.COUNTRIES as is for payments or derive it from the same table.

gaps.title: Organizer-side lookups by number (forget, person, unbind, mark, roster) have no country control
gaps.scenario: An organizer erasing or unbinding a foreign participant must type the number in a form that applies the same 10-digit rule; typing only the national part of an 8-9 digit country fails.
gaps.recommendation: Give these dialogs the same selector, or accept a '+cc...' string; they already hash on last 10 so no data change is needed.

gaps.title: Country table accuracy is unproven
gaps.scenario: The 244-row table was written from memory of ITU/libphonenumber rules; a wrong min or max would refuse a real number.
gaps.recommendation: Add the verification test in section F (libphonenumber-js example mobile numbers must fall inside every row's range, dial codes must match) before release; keep ranges wide where noted.

SCOPE AND METHOD
Read-only analysis of C:\ct\test-sites\tambola (HEAD 274bde8, release candidate 1.2.0; the only uncommitted change in the area is the check-in time format in z.js). Files read in full or in the relevant parts: edge people.ts, pii.ts, checkin.ts, winners.ts, rights.ts, lifecycle.ts, audit.ts, gamerecord.ts, consent.ts, the join / person / forget / roster / reuse / seats / prizes branches of worker.ts, web z.js, zgame.js (join call), consent.js, preview.js, rum.js, blackbox.js, storage-registry.json, report-layout.ts, privacy.html, terms.html, legal.html. Nothing was run.

1. WHAT THE JOIN PAGE ASKS TODAY (z.js joinWho L87-95, joinView L97-116)
Every join form carries: K4 two boxes (A: name+mobile used for this game only, deleted in 24 h, inviter recorded, winners kept 365 d; B: 18 or older), the fields below, the button "Get my ticket" (disabled until both boxes are ticked), and a line "We use your number for your ticket and, if you win, your prize. Your organizer sees it. Other players do not."
There is NO country picker, NO dial code, NO red asterisk, NO word "mandatory" and NO "(optional)" anywhere (grep of z.js: no country/optional/mandatory text; the only "dial" hits are "alertdialog"). Placeholder is always "98765 43210". The name box is always shown (except on a personal link) as "Your name (shown only to the organizer)" with no marker.

| mobile (default) | "Your mobile number"; name | phone 10-15 digits of anything; name optional |
| id + employeesOnly | "Your employee ID" + "This game is for employees only."; name. NO mobile field | ID (code need-id); name optional |
| id, not employeesOnly | ID; then "No employee ID? Type your mobile number instead" (hint: vendors, customers, families); name | ID or phone |
| either | mobile, "or", ID ("Give either one..."); name | at least one |
| both, not employeesOnly | mobile; "Your employee ID (employees only)" + "Not an employee? Leave this empty."; name | mobile; ID optional, but if the listed person has an ID it must match |
| both + employeesOnly | mobile; ID ("This game is for employees only."); name | both |
| personal link /j/<token> | no fields: "Your personal link is ready. Press the button"; name not asked | nothing typed; K4 |
| link used on another phone | mobile (+ID, name) with a banner asking for the number | number |

2. SERVER JOIN RULES (worker.ts L1558-1680) AND ERROR TEXTS
Order: token lookup (L1562) -> typed phone via digitsOf = ANY 10-15 digits, non-digits silently stripped (L1489, L1567-1569) -> employee ID via normEmp (ASCII A-Z0-9 . _ - /, max 30, upper-cased; else "An employee ID has letters and numbers only.") -> need-id checks (L1573-1574) -> either-mode ID lookup treats a listed ID like a personal link (L1575-1580) -> idOnly (L1581) -> ph = emp hash or phone hash (L1583) -> error "Enter your employee ID, or your mobile number if you have no employee ID." / "Enter your mobile number or your employee ID." / "Enter a valid mobile number." (L1584) -> K4 server check (L1585, L1627) -> device id mandatory ("Please refresh this page") (L1629) -> same-number/other-phone/device-used checks -> list lookup personByPhone (L1611) -> wrong-ID counter (30 per 10 min per network, L1616-1622) -> unlisted on a closed game or wrong ID: waiting room (L1665) -> otherwise seat. Listed person: the LIST's sealed record is used as-is, a typed name only fills a missing name (L1663); unlisted: new sealed record {phone as typed, name, empId only when mode is not mobile} (L1669).

3. PER USE CASE: CAPTURED, STORED, SEEN BY, KEPT
Common to all joins: seat(ph=salted hash of last 10 digits or employee-ID hash, dev=hash of the phone's random id, inv/src/cat = who invited and the guest kind chosen by the inviter), participant(phone_hash, pii sealed AES-GCM {p,n,e}), person row (second sealed copy, inviter, status), consent_log K4 row (opaque id, version, boxes A,B, wording hash, time), audit_log row with a sealed participant part (typed phone/name/ID as sent, full IP, user agent, raw device id; shredded 20 h after the game), kv counters keyed by an UNSALTED SHA-256 of the IP (jbm/jlim 2 days; idmiss never swept).
