| 13 Second phone / link already used | number asked again; else 423 other-phone | only a sealed audit row, shredded 20 h | organizer must unbind: console tool needs a MOBILE number |
| 14 Wrong input | no echo/confirm; 11-digit typos accepted; wrong number of a third party stored in waiting | audit row | approver sees last 4 of the wrong number |
Check-in (games created after 2026-10-23): shows Game ID, Participant ID, Ticket ID, name, mobile as ******1234, inviter's name; both "correct" ticks are mandatory even if no mobile/name exists; mobile edit accepts only Indian 10-digit; a name edit is written to the PLAINTEXT participant.name column (checkin.ts L107).
Winner confirmation: name AND mobile mandatory (winners.ts L85-87), mobile reduced to its last 10 digits, employee ID dropped from the record (L91); prize row keeps current pii, original join pii (orig) and every change (trail) for 365 days; the audit row of the 'prize' event keeps the typed name, phone, full IP, user agent and raw device id for 365 days (audit.ts L172, L267-273).

4. WHO CAN SEE WHAT
Organizer (master key) and Host (non-link): full lists, names of winners, prizes with orig and trail, report link, CSV of name+mobile+ID+personal link+WhatsApp link (waLink contains the full number, so the 'masked' view is cosmetic). Co-host: only people on its own list and waiting requests in its chain; cannot read prizes or report (can() excludes cohost, worker.ts L698). Level-1 guest: own invitees (name, masked number, waLink, personal link, empId) - AND ANYONE who knows the guest's pid (public, see G1). AI key / AI link: refused everywhere for names and numbers; prizes list has seats only (good). Other players: seat list, results, claims and the big screen carry opaque ids only (good), except inviter's name at check-in and first name/last 4 of requesters shown to guest approvers. Platform owner: everything.

5. MINIMUM-NECESSARY REVIEW
Demanded but not needed for that case: mobile at prize confirmation for an ID-only winner; ticks "this mobile number is correct" for a participant who has no mobile; K4 text about "name and mobile number" for ID-only games; full IP/UA/raw device id kept for winners' prize rows 365 days; declined/removed requesters' sealed details kept to game end; wrong-number requests never withdrawn.
Needed but not captured or not carried: country/dial code of a mobile; employee ID in the report, winners list, prize record and check-in (the only identifier of an ID-only winner); an optional mobile in employees-only/ID-only games; a no-identifier join mode; a way for a waiting person to withdraw.

6. LEGAL PAGES VS CODE (summary)
privacy.html L57/58 and K4 text mention only name and mobile (no employee ID, no check-in time, no IP/UA/raw device id in the security record, no waiting-room request); L58/Terms 11.3(c) say winners' confirmed name+number are kept, code also keeps the ORIGINAL details and the change trail; Terms 11.3(b) says security records are kept 'without Participant names or mobile numbers' for 365 days, but 'prize' audit rows hold them; legal.html L77 'Participants never see each other's data' vs inviter name at check-in, guest invitee list, approver first name/last 4; legal.html L60 says the ticket is marked for you and you do not need to claim (game requires tapping and Claim, z.js L179/L242); report-layout.ts L61 and lifecycle.ts L240-243 say the report holds ALL data held about people but it omits employee ID; Terms say K6 is 'not shown as a box' but the guest invite form shows it (z.js L510); winners are told the 'organizer and co-host' will see changes (z.js L315) while a Co-host cannot read prizes.

7. WHAT WORKS WELL (keep)
Names, numbers, IDs sealed AES-256-GCM; salted hashes for identity; K4 enforced on the server before anything is kept; list name wins over a typed name; employee ID not stored in mobile mode; AI refused for all personal data; participant audit part crypto-shredded at 20 h; check-in, prize, leave and data-request routes are bound to the ticket's own device; CSV formula guard; public seat list/results/big screen are anonymous; no cookies on game pages; blackbox/RUM scrub typed text; erasure job covers participant, seat, person, waiting, consent, check-in, report chunks.

8. TARGET SPEC FOR THE JOIN PAGE (to implement)
Legend line 'red * = mandatory (small word)'. Country select (default India +91) with per-country national length table, trunk-0 stripped, E.164 shown back ('We will use +91 98765 43210'). Matrix: mobile only: Mobile *mandatory, Name (optional). Employees only + ID only: Employee ID *mandatory, Mobile (optional), Name hidden/pre-announced if on file else asked. ID + mobile compulsory: both with red asterisk and 'mandatory'. Not-employees-only ID+mobile: Mobile mandatory, ID '(employees only, optional)'. ID or mobile: 'give at least one' on both. Personal link: no fields, show 'Playing as <first name>'. Anyone/no validation: Name (optional) only, identity from the device.

gaps.title: G1 Guest 'My invites' API is protected only by a PUBLIC ticket id: anyone can read invitees' names, numbers, ID and personal links, and act for the guest
gaps.scenario: Invitations are on (audiences 2 and 4). After the game starts the seat list GET /api/z/{id}/seats is public and lists every pid. A stranger with the game link calls GET /api/z/{id}/people?me=<pid of any direct participant> (also /waiting?me=). callerOf (L146-154) only checks that the pid exists, with no device proof, unlike checkin/myprizes/leave. The answer includes each invitee's name, masked phone, empId, the personal link token (/j/<token>, which lets the reader open that ticket first) and a wa.me link that contains the FULL mobile number (viewOf L166-176). The same pid lets the stranger POST waiting decisions and add people to that guest's quota. This contradicts 'Participants never see each other's data' and 'We do not show players' names or numbers to other players'.
gaps.recommendation: Require the ticket's device proof (x-ct-device hash equals seat.dev, as deviceMatches in checkin.ts) in callerOf for guests, on every method; stop returning link/waLink/full-digit data on list GETs (return them only in the add/resend response to the owning device); block guest list/waiting reads when the seat has no device; add a test that a request with only ?me=<pid> is refused.

gaps.title: G2 No country selection; numbers of other countries cannot be typed with their own length
gaps.scenario: A participant in Singapore (8 digits), Hong Kong (8), Denmark (8) or Israel (9) types their national number on the join page: digitsOf (worker.ts L1489) needs 10-15 digits, so it answers 'Enter a valid mobile number.' with no hint about a country code. There is no country select, the placeholder is always '98765 43210', and the guide only says 'Add the country code only if the person is outside India'. The identity is the last 10 digits only (worker.ts L1493, people.ts L48), so numbers of different countries can collide.
gaps.recommendation: Add a country select (default India +91) with per-country min/max national length, send cc + national (E.164), normalise on the server with one shared module used by join, people.ts cleanPhone, checkin, winners confirm and the console; hash E.164 (keep the existing last-10 hash for +91 so current lists still match); show the normalised number back before submitting.

gaps.title: G3 No mandatory / optional marking on any field
gaps.scenario: Owner requirement: red asterisk plus the small word 'mandatory' where both employee ID and mobile are compulsory, '(optional)' for the mobile in ID-only games. The join form shows plain labels ('Your mobile number', 'Your employee ID', 'Your name (shown only to the organizer)') in every mode; the person learns what is required only from a server error after pressing the button.
gaps.recommendation: Render the matrix in section 8 of the findings: red * and the word 'mandatory' on required fields, '(optional)' on optional ones, aria-required/required attributes, a one-line legend, and client-side checks that mirror the server rules (need-id, either, both).

gaps.title: G4 ID-only games: mobile cannot be given as optional, and an ID plus a typed mobile sends a listed employee to the waiting room
gaps.scenario: (a) verify=id with employeesOnly: the page shows no mobile field at all (z.js L91), although the owner wants an optional mobile. (b) verify=id, not employeesOnly: the page offers a mobile box; a listed employee who types BOTH ID and mobile gets ph = phone hash (idOnly is false because typedGiven, L1581-1583), personByPhone finds nothing (list rows of ID-only people are keyed by the ID hash, people.ts L290-295), idMiss is set (L1615), the wrong-ID counter is bumped and the employee lands in the waiting room even though the ID is on the list. A shared office network also hits the 30-per-10-minutes limit.
gaps.recommendation: In id and either modes treat a typed ID as the identity whenever it is present and keep the typed mobile only as optional contact data in the sealed record; show an '(optional)' mobile in ID-only/employees-only games; do not count a lookup as a miss when the ID is on the list.

gaps.title: G5 Employee ID is captured but never shown in the report, winners list, prize record or check-in, and the report claims to hold ALL data
gaps.scenario: An ID-only game ends. ReportPerson, ReportWinner, listPrizes and the check-in page carry name and phone only (empId is referenced only in people.ts, worker.ts join, checkin edit pass-through, pii.ts). The report text says 'We have given you ALL the data we hold about the people' (report-layout.ts L61) and the e-mail says it is the only copy; 20 hours later the IDs are gone with the people rows. A winner who gave only an ID is '(no name)' with a blank mobile in the PDF and the organizer cannot tell which employee won.
gaps.recommendation: Carry empId through ReportPerson/ReportWinner/listPrizes/prize rows/check-in (read-only line 'Employee ID'), add an 'Employee ID' column to the report when verify is not mobile, and keep the text 'ALL the data' true.

gaps.title: G6 Winner confirmation forces name and a valid mobile for everyone, cuts the country code and drops the employee ID
gaps.scenario: An employee joined with an ID only. After winning, confirmCard (z.js L310-319) requires 'Your mobile number'; the server answers 'Please enter a valid mobile number.' if it is not 10-15 digits (L28, L87), then stores only the last 10 digits (L28) and seals {phone,name} without empId (L91), so a +44 or +65 winner's number loses its country code and the ID is erased from the current record. changed is always true for ID-only winners, which prints 'joined as ?, ?' in the report.
gaps.recommendation: Make the mobile optional when the winner joined without one, show the employee ID read-only, keep the full E.164 number, keep empId in the sealed record, and compute 'changed' only on real differences.

gaps.title: G7 Check-in is India-only for mobile edits and forces confirmation of data that was never captured
gaps.scenario: A participant outside India clicks Edit on the mobile box: digits are stripped of 91/0 and must match /^[6-9]\d{9}$/ (L103-104), so a UK, SG or US number gives 'The mobile number needs 10 digits' (guide.js repeats 'A mobile number has 10 digits'); ckmob is maxlength 14. An ID-only participant with no mobile and no name must still tick 'This mobile number is correct' and 'This name is correct' (L88, z.js L724-727). An edit that re-types the same Indian number is flagged as changed because the stored value has 91 and the typed one does not, and the stored number silently loses the 91.
gaps.recommendation: Use the shared international phone module, skip the mobile/name confirmation rows when none is held (or make them 'add if you wish'), compare normalised numbers, and keep the stored format.

gaps.title: G8 Winners' 'prize' audit rows keep typed name, phone, full IP, user agent and raw device id for 365 days; the notices say otherwise
gaps.scenario: splitsPersonal exempts events starting with 'prize' (confirm, prizegiven), so the whole details object (ip, ua, device_id and changes {pid, name, phone}; 'phone' and 'name' are not redacted, SECRET_KEY L43) is sealed into audit_log and kept until the 365-day cleanup. Terms 11.3(b) say security records are kept 'without Participant names or mobile numbers'; privacy.html L71 says the players' personal part is destroyed at 20 hours; privacy L57 says the phone id is kept 'only as a scrambled code'. A winner's leave/erasure (rights.ts) clears prize.pii but not these rows.
gaps.recommendation: Store prize events in the shreddable participant part (or drop name/phone/IP/device_id from them), keep only seat, time and result for 365 days, or state the exact retention in the privacy page and K4.

gaps.title: G9 No identifier-free join mode: 'anyone can join' still demands a mobile number or an employee ID
gaps.scenario: The owner's list includes 'none of the above / anyone can join'. verify can only be mobile, id, either or both (config.ts L313-315) and the join refuses without ph (L1584). A person who does not want to give any number cannot play although one ticket per phone could rest on the device id alone.
gaps.recommendation: If the owner wants this, add verify 'none': ph = hash(eid|device), name optional, mobile asked only at prize confirmation; label the page 'Nothing is needed to join'. If not, say so in the console so organizers do not expect it.

gaps.title: G10 Check-in name edit is written to a plaintext column
gaps.scenario: UPDATE participant SET pii=?, name=? stores the corrected name in clear in participant.name (join writes NULL). Everyone who edits a name at check-in has a readable name in the database until 20 h after the game, contradicting pii.ts ('never stored in the clear') and legal.html 'All data is encrypted, in transit and at rest'.
gaps.recommendation: Write name=NULL there (the sealed pii already holds it) and read only from pii; add a test that participant.name is never non-null.

gaps.title: G11 Waiting room keeps wrong, third-party and declined details and offers no withdrawal
gaps.scenario: A person mistypes one digit on a list game: that other person's number is sealed into a waiting row and shown to approvers (last 4). The button 'Wrong number or ID? Type it again' (z.js L100, L823) only resets the screen: the first request stays and the approver now sees two. A declined request keeps its sealed phone/name/ID until 20 h after the game (possibly weeks). A waiting person has no pid, so leave/datareq cannot be used; the typed values also sit in localStorage for 7 days (z.js L136).
gaps.recommendation: Add DELETE of a waiting request by wid (+ device), call it from 'Type it again', erase pii on decline, add a 'Withdraw my request' button, show the typed number back for confirmation before submit, and clear the localStorage record on any exit.

gaps.title: G12 Organizer 'forget this person' leaves the person and waiting rows and works by mobile number only
gaps.scenario: The forget action deletes participant, seat, K4, claims, bogeys and prize pii but not the person row (sealed name, phone, empId, token) nor a waiting row, so the data and the working personal link remain until the purge; rights.ts leaveStatements handles the person row correctly. Both person/forget and the console tools 'Look up', 'Change of phone' (zc.js L764) call phoneHash, so an ID-only participant (ph = ID hash) cannot be found, forgotten or unbound there.
gaps.recommendation: Reuse leaveStatements for forget; accept seat number or employee ID in person, forget and unbind; add tests for ID-only people.

gaps.title: G13 Name field: unlabelled, inaccurate promise, never asked on a personal link, always asked when already on file
gaps.scenario: The label says 'shown only to the organizer' but Hosts see it, guests see their invitees', approvers see first names and invitees see the inviter's name. A person on a personal link is never asked for a name (L110 'personal ? ""'), so a list without names yields '(no name)' until prize time. A person whose name the organizer already supplied is still asked (the server ignores the typed name, L1663), and nothing tells them whose name will be used.
gaps.recommendation: Label it '(optional)' or '*mandatory' per organizer choice, say 'If your organizer already has your name it is used', show 'Playing as <name>' after joining, and ask the name on a personal link only when none is on file (a safe yes/no from the join reply, not a lookup before consent).

gaps.title: G14 Join accepts looser input than the list side and does not echo the number back
gaps.scenario: people.ts cleanPhone rejects letters and requires Indian numbers to start with 6-9, while join digitsOf strips every non-digit and accepts any 10-15 digits: '98765432101' (extra digit) or '9876543210 ext 5' pass, hash differently, and end in the waiting room or on a wrong seat; the stored phone keeps the typed shape (leading 0, 91 or none), so the report mixes formats.
gaps.recommendation: Use one validator for join, list and check-in; reject letters; show 'We will use +91 98765 43210, is that right?'; store E.164.

gaps.title: G15 Notices and consent text omit what is really collected
gaps.scenario: The player section and K4-A name only name and mobile number. Not mentioned: employee ID (Terms 1.6 and 11.4A mention IDs only for lists), the waiting-room request, the check-in time kept 365 days for winners, the IP/browser/raw device id in the sealed security record, the original-join copy and change trail of winner details (privacy L58 says only 'the name and mobile number you confirm'), the guest kind chosen by the inviter. K4 says 'my name and mobile number' to an ID-only participant who typed neither. heldAbout (rights.ts L110-126) answers 'what do you hold' without ID, consent record, security record or waiting/person copies.
gaps.recommendation: Rewrite privacy L57-58, K4-A (version bump in consent.js, consent-text.json, terms table) and heldAbout so they list every item above; vary K4-A wording by verify mode.

gaps.title: G16 Statements in legal pages that the code contradicts
gaps.scenario: 'Participants never see each other's data' (L77) vs inviter name at check-in (checkin.ts L79) and guest invitee lists; L60 'The software marks each called number... You do not need to claim' vs tap-and-Claim play (z.js L179, L242); Terms L55/L77 'K6 is not shown as a box' vs the box in the guest form (z.js L510); winners told the 'co-host' sees changes (z.js L315) while Co-host cannot read prizes; report/e-mail 'ALL data' vs missing employee ID.
gaps.recommendation: Correct each sentence (version-date the pages), or change the behaviour; add a test that links the quoted promises to code checks.

gaps.title: G17 Whoever types a listed number or listed employee ID first gets that person's ticket and sees their name and last 4 digits
gaps.scenario: A typed number is only matched, not proven (people.ts header). A colleague who types another listed person's number (or ID in either mode) before they do binds the seat to his device and then sees the listed full name and ******1234 on the check-in page, and later the winner's details through myprizes/confirm. The real person gets link-used / other-phone.
gaps.recommendation: Show the listed name only after a proof (personal link token or organizer approval), or ask for a second factor already on the list (last 4 of ID/mobile); at least alert the organizer when a listed person is claimed by a device without the personal link.

gaps.title: G18 International numbers in lists without '+' are read as Indian
gaps.scenario: cleanPhone treats any 10-digit number starting 6-9 as Indian: a Singapore number '6581234567' (65 + 8 digits) is stored as +91 6581234567, so the WhatsApp invitation goes to the wrong number; 8-9 digit national numbers are 'too short' (L76).
gaps.recommendation: Per-country table plus an explicit country column or default-country setting for the list upload.

gaps.title: G19 Unsalted IP hashes are kept: idmiss never swept, jbm/jlim 2 days, none disclosed
gaps.scenario: Counters are keyed by sha256('jip|'+IP) first 16 hex without secret (L391, L1618): an IPv4 space is guessable in seconds, so it is effectively the address. idmiss/<eid>/<time>/<hash> is not in retentionSweep (L2053 covers start/ linkfail/ plim/ jlim/ jbm/ only), nor in erasePersonal/deleteEngagementRows, so it is never deleted; privacy.html mentions none of these counters.
gaps.recommendation: Salt with a server secret, add idmiss/ to the sweep and to erasePersonal, and mention the 2-day network counters in the privacy page.

gaps.title: G20 Approvers (Co-host, guest) get no identifier for ID-only requests
gaps.scenario: listWaiting shows firstName and last4 to non-Host approvers and the empId only to Organizer/Host. A request made with an ID and no name or phone shows a blank row to a Co-host or guest who has the right to admit it.
gaps.recommendation: Show a masked ID (first/last characters) or route ID-only requests to Organizer/Host.

gaps.title: G21 Legacy roster/reuse paths copy people between games without the 'this game only' consent
gaps.scenario: reuse copies the sealed records of an earlier game (while they still exist) into a new game, with no K4 and no organizer confirmation, against K4-A 'used for this game only'; can() (L698) lets an AI key reach it (it cannot read the data but can move it). roster is mobile-only and ignores employee IDs. The console has handler code but no rendered button.
gaps.recommendation: Remove both routes or require K6 and a participant K4 on first open; refuse AI keys.

gaps.title: G22 Full list/CSV downloads of names, numbers and personal links are not audited
gaps.scenario: classify() logs GET people/export as nothing (audit.ts L141); an Organizer or Host can download every number and every ticket link and nothing records who did it or when.
gaps.recommendation: Add an 'export' event with actor, count and time (no content).

gaps.title: G23 Participant sees another participant's name
gaps.scenario: 'You came in through <inviter name>' puts one player's name on another player's phone; first name and last 4 of requesters go to guest approvers; contradicts 'We do not show players' names or numbers to other players' (privacy L64).
gaps.recommendation: Show 'your inviter' without a name, or adjust the policy text.

gaps.title: G24 Waiting-room record on the phone is not described in the device notice
gaps.scenario: ctz-wait-<eid> holds the typed mobile, employee ID, name and request id for up to 7 days; storage-registry.json lists the key but its plain-words sentence (and legal.html) talk only about ticket, taps, prizes and an unfinished check-in.
gaps.recommendation: Add the sentence 'the details typed while waiting for approval, up to 7 days' and clear it when the page is closed or the request ends.

gaps.title: G25 Erasure after the game does not touch the already-built report copy, yet says 'deleted just now'
gaps.scenario: leaveStatements/takeOut remove participant, seat, person, prize pii but not the sealed kv rptc/<eid>/n chunks nor the 'prize' audit rows; the organizer's report link (open to 19 h) still lists the person.
gaps.recommendation: Say so in the answer, or mark the person removed in the chunks.

gaps.title: G26 Identity is the last 10 digits with a fallback salt of 'unset'
gaps.scenario: Two people in different countries with the same last 10 digits are one person ('same number twice = same participant', then 423 for the second); if PHONE_SALT and ORGANIZER_SECRET are both missing the hash uses 'unset' and the public pid (a hash of it, worker.ts L1495) becomes brute-forceable.
gaps.recommendation: Hash E.164, refuse to start without PHONE_SALT, add a deployment check.

gaps.title: G27 Employee ID format is ASCII-only and name cleaning at join is weaker than elsewhere
gaps.scenario: IDs with non-ASCII letters or other symbols are rejected ('letters and numbers only'); worker.ts cleanName (L1508) removes only < > ` and truncates, while people.ts and checkin.ts also drop control, bidi and formula-leading characters, so a join name can carry them into the report.
gaps.recommendation: Allow Unicode letters/digits in IDs, use the strict name cleaner everywhere.

analyses.findings:
SCOPE AND METHOD
Read-only. I read the tests under apps/edge/test (about 77 files), apps/web/test (31), packages/beacon/test (16), tests/e2e, the tools in C:\ct\test-sites\tools (identical copies live in tambola\tools\load-tests and browser-tests; hot\ and wt-tools\ are stale copies; only ui-permute.mjs differs by one line) and tambola\tools\sim2. Nothing was run, so "exists" means a test is present in the working tree (HEAD 274bde8, 1.2.0 candidate), not that it passes. Uncommitted files (z.js check-in locale, local.ts latency knobs, nodephone IP_POOL, start-tambola.ps1) do not touch joining. The Grep tool silently dropped files on directory-wide searches (verify.test.ts was missing), so every "no test does X" claim below was re-checked with grep -rl.

HEADLINE
1. Not one test of the participant join form touches an employee-ID mode. grep -rl for #emp, empId, "Your employee ID" over apps/web/test finds only organizer-console tests (pages.test.ts 1066/1285/1813, idiotproof-steps-5-6.test.ts 80). packages/beacon/test, tests/e2e and tambola/tools/sim2 have zero ID coverage. ID joins are tested only at the API level (apps/edge/test/verify.test.ts, 17 tests) and by protocol phones (campaign.mjs, sigma-http.mjs); real pages only by hand-run ui-game.mjs (live runs: audience 1 and 5 only, per data/ui/live-matrix.summary).
2. The two headline requirements have no code and no tests. z.js has no country picker and no mandatory/optional marks (zero matches for country, dial, optional, mandatory in z.js and z.html). The only field logic is joinWho(), z.js 87-95.
3. While designing the matrix I found a probable defect (read from code, not executed): with verify=id, a listed employee who types BOTH ID and mobile is sent to the waiting room, and it burns the 30-per-10-minutes ID-miss budget. This becomes the common case once the form shows an "(optional)" mobile next to the ID. No test would catch it.

WHAT THE JOIN DOES TODAY (anchor for the tests)
Form (z.js 87-116): mobile mode: one field "Your mobile number" (#ph, placeholder 98765 43210). id: "Your employee ID" (#emp, maxlength 30) plus, only when NOT employees-only, "No employee ID? Type your mobile number instead". either: mobile, the word "or", ID, hint "Give either one". both: mobile + ID ("Not an employee? Leave this empty." when not employees-only). Name box (#nm, "Your name (shown only to the organizer)") is always shown unless a personal link; no label says optional or mandatory; no asterisks; no country list. Two consent boxes (K4) gate the button.
Server (worker.ts 1558-1680): digitsOf needs 10-15 digits and ignores the Indian 6-9 rule (1489); identity hash = last 10 digits (1493); ID-only identity = empHash (1581-1583); need-id 400 in employees-only (1573-1574); either: ID looked up before phone (1575-1580); both: ID checked against the listed one (1614); wrong or unlisted ID or number in a list game goes to waiting 403 (1613-1623, 1665); employees-only forces a closed list and switches guest invites off (1406, 2009; config.ts 332); typed name is used only if the list has none (1663, 1669); a personal link bypasses every ID check (1573, 1613).

EXISTING TESTS THAT TOUCH JOINING (by layer)
Server (bun, in-memory D1):
- verify.test.ts: normEmp unit (:39); settings saved and kept (:45, :52); employees-only ID alone (:65); employees-only mobile+ID (:81); ID stays after resend (:92); either (:102, :115, :123); list junk (:131); ID guessing limit 30 then 429 (:140); everyone+ID (:150); everyone+both (:158); mobile default ignores ID (:169); CSV has ID column (:177).

- worker.test.ts: join answer shape incl. verify/employeesOnly keys (:51-56); same number two ways (:58); hostile input (:70); cap (:89); seats and one-device rules (:814-864); late joiners.
- usecases.test.ts UC-28..UC-35 (:338-384); param-people.test.ts (list phone formats :11-64 are LIST adds, not joins; device rules :103-117; invitation policies :121-189); abuse.test.ts (per-IP limits); consent.test.ts K4 (:61, :109, :120); privacy.test.ts invitations (:85-140); roles.test.ts (:155); cancel/unplayed/checkin/rights for state gates.
Page (happy-dom, real z.js against real worker):
- phone-guest.test.ts: personal link, no fields (:93); link used on another phone (:102); unlisted waits and gets in on admit (:112); waiting survives reload (:122); declined (:135); removed (:142, :157); cancelled (:164); My invites (:173, :190).
- idiotproof-player-pages.test.ts: second-phone refusal wording and empty box (:45); waiting card "Type it again" (:59, phone only).
- consent-pages.test.ts :36 (K4 boxes gate the button, mobile game); pages.test.ts :772-816 guest invitation link UI-INV3 (banner, 5th guest told invite-full); :373/:1273 organizer "Who is this game for" (settings only).

DECISIONS TAKEN WHERE THE REQUIREMENTS LEAVE ROOM (each can be changed without rework)
D1 Anyone/no validation: mobile stays the one mandatory field, name optional, ID hidden. A real "no contact" mode would key identity on the device, which breaks "second phone" recovery; offer it later as its own project.
D2 Length policy: India is hard (exactly 10 digits, first digit 6-9). Every other country is checked against its national length range from the table and a mismatch is a SOFT stop: the message names the country and the count and says "press the button again if it is right". The second press with the same text goes through. A wrong table row can therefore never lock a real person out. Only 8-15 digits in all (country code included) is a hard rule.
D3 Name: the Name box is always shown as [O] with the hint. The server uses the list name when it has one and returns the first name, so the ticket greets "Welcome, Asha". Phase 2 (owner choice): hide the box once the ID is entered, using a guarded lookup (needs the consent ticks in the request, counts hits as well as misses per network, returns a first name only). For personal links, a lookup by token is safe (token is a secret) and shows "Hi <first name>".
D4 Unknown employee ID in an open game: keep today's behaviour (waiting room, so the organizer decides) but say so truthfully, and fix the console sentence "You do not need to approve anyone" for ID games.
D5 Guest link in a list-only game: until the owner chooses, tell the truth on the ticket card and the invitation text ("your guest asks to join and is let in by you or the organizer"). Option for later: a valid guest link inside the guest's quota counts as validation.
D6 Identity hash stays "last 10 digits" in 1.2.x (live rosters depend on it). Phase 2: hash full number for non-India numbers with a dual lookup.

WRONG INPUT: exact messages (client shows them under the box at once and sends nothing; the server returns the same words for hand-made requests)
- Mobile blank, mandatory: "Please type your mobile number."
- Letters or symbols: "A mobile number has digits only. You can use spaces, + and -."
- India, wrong count: "An Indian mobile number has 10 digits. You typed 9. Please check it."
- India, first digit: "An Indian mobile number starts with 6, 7, 8 or 9."
- Other country, count outside its range (soft): "A mobile number in Singapore usually has 8 digits. You typed 7. Please check it. If it is right, press the button again."
- Total digits outside 8-15: "That does not look like a mobile number. Please check the country and the digits."
- Unknown +code: "We do not know that country code. Please pick your country from the list."
- ID blank: "Please type your employee ID." Both blank: "Please type your employee ID and your mobile number." Either blank: "Please type your employee ID or your mobile number."
- ID bad characters or too long: "An employee ID can have letters, numbers and . _ - / only, up to 30 characters."
- ID not on list: waiting card (row 14), never a red error.
- Boxes not ticked: the button stays off and the hint says which box is left.
- Game full: "This game is full. Please ask your organizer." Busy (429/503): "Many people are joining right now. Please wait a moment and press the button again." with a Try again button.

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (ordered; each step ends green before the next; the laptop is short of memory, so run test files in groups, one process at a time, and never start a browser and a test run together)

STEP 0 - Protect what exists
- Take a snapshot commit of the uncommitted tree on a new branch (do not stash, do not revert): z.js, z.css, worker.ts, local.ts, nodephone.mjs, start-tambola.ps1, join-probe.test.ts. Confirm no other session is editing the same files before the first edit.
- Treat join-probe.test.ts as scaffolding: its five scenarios become real assertions in Step 6, then the file is deleted.

STEP 1 - One phone module (single source of truth)
- Create packages/beacon/src/dial.ts with the table [iso, name, dial, minNational, maxNational, trunk, zeroStays, firm] plus parse(iso, typed), validate(), show(), mask(). Seed it from the countries-phone report's 244-row table and the 229 rows now inline in z.js. The report's ranges are from memory: mark `firm` only where the length is fixed and well known (IN 10, US/CA/NANP 10, GB 10, SG 8, HK 8, AE 9, SA 9, AU 9, FR 9, ES 9, NL 9, PK 10, BD 10, LK 9, NP 10, CN 11, JP 10, PH 10, TH 9, ZA 9, NG 10, KE 9, EG 10, QA/KW/BH/OM 8, IL 9, TR 10, MX 10), everything else wide. Trunk fields: 0 default, 8 for RU/KZ/BY/UZ/TM/LT, 06 for HU, none for IT/BJ/GA/CG/CI (zero stays).
- Build it to apps/web/public/dial.js with the same pattern as zgame.js; import dial.ts directly in the Worker and in checkin.ts/winners.ts. Wire the new file in: pages/build.mjs FILES (a file missing there is silently NOT shipped), zsw.js FILES, script tags in z.html and zc.html, and the file list in apps/edge/test/ai-mail.test.ts:114. z.js stops carrying its own copy (remove CT_ROWS and CTPhone body; keep window.CTPhone as a thin alias so nothing else breaks).
- Keep India behaviour exactly as in the tree (10 digits, 6-9). Non-India: policy D2 (soft stop on a firm-range mismatch; hard only outside 8-15 digits in all).
- Do NOT change the hash (last 10 digits).

STEP 2 - Server join contract (backwards compatible; field names, status codes and `code` values do not change)
a) digitsOf: a number typed with + or 00 goes through dial.ts (known code, 8-15 digits, India held to 10 and 6-9). A bare number keeps the 1.1.8 rule (10-15 digits). This keeps older open pages and the protocol phones in tools/load-tests (which send phone, name, empId, device, consent with bare 10-digit numbers) behaving exactly as before.
b) Store country-code digits for every new join (bare 10 digits starting 6-9 get 91 in front); readers that build wa.me links tolerate old 10-digit rows.
c) Admitted is final: before computing idMiss, look for a waiting row for this identity with status admitted and skip the ID-mismatch/idMiss rule for it (fixes G4); wait() never answers "waiting" for an admitted row.
d) ID-miss counter moves after the consent check and only on the first sight of a distinct (network, ID); limit read from a variable with today's 30 as default.
e) Messages: waiting reply for an ID miss gets the truthful text and an extra field reason:"id-unlisted" (status 403, code "waiting", waiting:true, wid, with all unchanged). need-id and "Enter a valid mobile number." get an extra field ("id" or "mobile") so the page can mark the right box; the text becomes mode-specific ("Enter your employee ID and your mobile number." for both+ID-only).
f) Join reply (success) gains optional nameOnFile (bool) and firstName; nothing existing is removed.
g) Open game, Co-host/guest quota full: fall back to the organizer instead of waiting (G17). List game unchanged.
h) cleanName reuses the people.ts cleaner (G24). Game-full answer gets code "full".
i) Phase 2, behind owner choice: POST /api/z/:id/who (token or ID+consent) for the name echo; guarded as described in D3.

STEP 3 - Participant page (z.js, z.css, guide.js)
a) Keep the tree's joinNeeds/markOf layout; make the copy come from the mode: step 2 text, footer, invited-by banner by owner kind, needPhone text; read whoCanJoin and the game name from /info; add the one "who can join" line.
b) Country list: show name and +code (flags are decoration only; Windows desktops draw letters), India first, remembered per phone (ctz-cc), placeholder and live hint from the table ("India: 10 digits"), soft-stop logic for D2 (remember the text that was warned; the same text on the second press is sent). Preview line "We will use +65 9123 4567".
c) Mark the two consent boxes [M]; add aria-describedby/aria-invalid and an inline message under the offending box; data-need on every mandatory input so guide.js can name what is missing.
d) needPhone: omit the token when the person typed an ID and no mobile (G10).
e) Persist typed country/number/ID/name in sessionStorage; focus guard on any focused input (G20).
f) Waiting poll with jitter and back-off; "Type it again" calls a withdraw; handle state gone (G19).
g) guide.js: data-ctg-skip on the waiting/declined/lapsed/removed/gone cards, honoured in okToUpgrade and leafMessage; player wording for "by invitation" that says "wait"; mode-neutral wording for the mobile and ID guides ("Type your mobile number with its country", no "10-digit", no "outside India"); Try again button for busy answers (G27).
